items.label: No. 101
items.sum: Editorial on the first full post-war winter season, urging the club to build a strong track team before the 1948 London Olympics, with news of Southern Championship wins by Len Herbert and Derrick Burfitt.
items.s: Editorial Editorial on the first full post-war winter season, urging the club to build a strong track team before the 1948 London Olympics, with news of Southern Championship wins by Len Herbert and Derrick Burfitt. We are now at the end of what can be termed the first full post-war winter season. From the afternoon of the season's opening meeting at Belgrave Hall the atmosphere was set: time seemed to have slipped back and the years of the war became, in many minds, non-existent. As one who "arrived back" that afternoon not having been near Belgrave Hall since 1940, it was a startling joy to see again so many well-remembered faces and to be greeted with such a warmth of welcome. Many things have changed these past seven years and this club has lost some of its dearest and best members, but we are still a club with enthusiasm and unity about us. At present most things are opposed, or unhelpful, towards the pursuit of Athletics. This country, unlike many others, gives no official or material support to Amateur Sports Clubs of any kind. Whether this is for better or for worse is a debateable question, but it is our heritage that such clubs as ours should be free to control and run their pursuits without any outside interference or aid, therefore what we achieve can verily be called our own. We have much to achieve, both for the benefit of the Athletic world in general and for the glory of this Club. The task of this Club in the future must be to build a strong, thoroughly ALL-ROUND Club, setting an example of fair sportsmanship that will make our name a byword for such things and influencing all those who have contact with the Club. In 1948 the Olympic Games will be held in London. Between now and then it must be our object to build a Track team as strong as our Walking and Country teams have been for so many years. If we can achieve such eminence in these two spheres there is no good reason why we should not do likewise on the track. We have the talent, some of it already shown, some of it dormant, but to mention only these few names is to comment on a strength which could do much: Broadbent, Botwright, Burfitt, Blowfield, Nankeville, Marchant, Herbert, Read, Lucas, Stimpson. To reach our object on the track our training must be made more rigorous, new methods must be tried, progress must be noted and used to advantage, and above all we must train together and help each other. It is the only way that standards can be compared and raised. Such must be our objects. They have in turn a more profound aspect, for Athletics is one of the few truly amateur sports left. It requires much selfless endeavour for no material gain and it can only be successfully pursued if loved, and to love it is to love something outside yourself. Thus it helps to form an essentially unneurotic outlook in a world where the selfish and neurotic is ever more shrill and powerful in its beseeching. To help counter this modern disease even in our small way, is to achieve something of a rare sanity these days. Whilst this Edition is in progress the Southern C.C. Championship has been run. Len Herbert ran a magnificent race to win the Senior race, and Derrick Burfitt found a fine finish to win the Junior race. A weakened team in the Seniors were second to Aylesford Paper Mills and the Junior team ran very well to finish third to S.L.H. and T.V.H. items.sum: Obituary of walker Ted Jackman, a member since 1930, who died aged 35.
items.s: Obituary Obituary of walker Ted Jackman, a member since 1930, who died aged 35. It is with the greatest regret that we have to announce the death of TED JACKMAN at the early age of 35 years. Ted joined us in 1930 and quickly showed that he had walking ability. During the summer of 1931 he was placed frequently in Club Track Handicaps and, improving apace, was successful in Open Track Handicaps, his win in the Ponders End Fete and Gala being particularly memorable. His walking on the road also showed improvement, and although never attaining championship rank he was always a dependable club man. His personality was pleasing. A gentle modest bearing, combined with sterling character and excellent sportsmanship endeared him to all, and he will be sorely missed, for we can ill afford to lose such a splendid club man. Only the day before his death he was talking of his many friends within the Club, of which he has been a proud member for seventeen years. We are the richer for his friendship and loyalty, the poorer for his passing at such an early age. Frank Elson, Charlie Churcher and Charlie Poulter paid the Club's last respects at the funeral, and a wreath in Club colours testified to the esteem in which he was held. Our profound sympathy is extended to Ted's parents and sister in their very great loss. items.label: No. 101
items.sum: Club news column: Surrey C.C. Championship win and county colours, walking successes, Britannia Shield race, South of Thames races and Coleman Cup, Olympic hopes, and notes on individual members.
items.s: Commentary Club news column: Surrey C.C. Championship win and county colours, walking successes, Britannia Shield race, South of Thames races and Coleman Cup, Olympic hopes, and notes on individual members. On page 6 will be found a short note from the Hon. Treasurer, Bill Webb. It is hoped that any guilty members will take note of the paragraph on subscription. Dave Martin Shepard and the Social Committee are doing great work now and are putting the Belgrave social side on its feet again. The repairs to Belgrave Hall have been completed and its use for frolics in the future will be as deplorable as ever was! The Belgrave News Letter, edited and printed by Frank Elson, is at its 69th Edition. It is a very well edited Letter and the idea behind it a sound one, for it does keep all members of the Walking Section in the closest touch with the doings (or would you prefer the word "victories," Frank!), of this illustrious Section. The Club Annual Dinner was most successful. The attendance was a record, the speeches complementary to all and not too long, the food good and the party spirit most excellent. We won the Surrey C.C. Championship again and Cadogan A.C. (our friends) were third in the Middlesex. Surrey Colours were won by Tom Carter, Len Herbert, Bill Lucas and Leslie Stokell. Middlesex Colours by Vic Blowfield and Geoffry Pearson. In the Kent Championships George Lucas was 5th and in the Herts. Championship Albert Frost was 4th. Both these Belgravians won their County Colours. War-time members Jimmy Green and Peter Moughan won their County Colours for Kent and Herts. respectively. Congratulations to our Junior Captain, Eddy Short, who was 4th in the London University C.C. Championships: George Lucas, 3rd in the North Kent District Race; Geoffry Pearson, 2nd in the Banks Championship. The Walking Section is winning everything at present in a most glorious fashion. All the big Southern "Opens" have fallen to us and Harry Churcher, closely followed by Jack Rutland, has once again proved himself unbeatable over his distances. The National races are yet to come, but we can own a measure of confidence in our ability to do well in these. In the Britannia Shield race last November, Len Herbert, running for the R.A.F., was 5th and 2nd Englishman home. Our Belgian friend and member, Etienne Gailly, was 7th, running for the Belgian Army, and our Poly member, Dick Towndrow, 15th, running for the British Army team. This Club extends its most sincere congratulations to Mr. E. J. Holt, of S.L.H., on his being made an Officer of the Order of the British Empire for his services to Athletics, which have indeed been great. We won the South of Thames "Junior." Bill Lucas and Len Marchant ran fine races to finish 1st and 2nd. In the South of the Thames "Senior" we were 2nd. Our score of 87 points, the lowest ever recorded for 2nd place, would normally have won us the race. Our congratulations go to the Aylesford Club, who turned out such a good performance to beat us. We won the Coleman Cup for the lowest score for 12 men home. Michael Broadbent and Derrick Burfitt have been mentioned in the press as being British Olympic hopes. We believe they can do it given the chances, and we hope others will join them by 1948. In view of the above it is interesting to note that Derrick, and Arthur Bruce, are awaiting their call up any moment now. Your Hon. Editor is receiving copies of The Scots Athlete. This is a first-class journal dealing very fully with events over the border. It makes extremely good reading. It is published by W. J. Ross at 69 St. Vincent Street, Glasgow, C.2. Annual subscription 6/6. It is good to see Arthur Penny running again and running as well as ever. Such veterans as Arthur are the salt of this club and the fact that they can come back, when not far short of 40 years, tells that past training has been good. All younger running members can learn a thing or two from such as Arthur. Ted Stimpson has recovered from his operation and is training again. We give Ted our best wishes for the future Track season—and what about the 1948 Olympic 10,000 metres, Ted? We were pleased to see Dick Murphy starting the Ten Mile Walk and presenting his shield to the winner, Harry Churcher. No mention was made in the Handbook of the winning by P. J. Briggs of the Surrey Junior Hurdles Championship last season. This was a most regrettable omission and we give our apologies to Briggs, who is now serving in the Army, and is stationed at Larkhill. Victor Blowfield is showing international form over the country. His winning of the Club Ten was magnificent. With good training Vic is going to be a menace to the best in the country during the next Track season. Also congratulations to a new member, Leslie Stokell, on his fine and ever-improving running this season. There are also big things in store for Les in the future. This column would like to see him try the 2 miles Steeplechase next summer. Bill Webb Bill Webb Hon. items.label: No. 101
items.sum: Hon. Treasurer's notes on when subscriptions fall due, juniors on National Service, damage to and engraving of club trophies, engraving of medals, and badges.
items.s: Hon. Treasurer's Notes Hon. Treasurer's notes on when subscriptions fall due, juniors on National Service, damage to and engraving of club trophies, engraving of medals, and badges. SUBSCRIPTIONS. Some misunderstanding appears to exist as to the date on which the club Annual Subscription becomes due. A number of members have assumed that the club Financial Year runs concurrently with the calendar year and that January 1st is the date on which subscriptions are due; others have regarded the date of their election to Membership as the governing date for payment. The clarification of this point is best served by a reference to rules 7 and 9 on pages 18 and 19 of the handbook, where it clearly states that the club financial year ends on September 15th and that subscriptions become due and payable on the date of the Annual General Meeting. It is important that outstanding subscriptions should be paid immediately. The normal running expenses of the club have to be met and a reference to the last balance sheet will show that they are no mean liability. Subscriptions should be forwarded or handed to the Hon. Treasurer. Alternatively they may be handed to the Assistant Hon. Treasurer, Mr. T. F. Morrell, or, in the case of walking members, to the Hon. Walking Secretary, Mr. S. Roberts. The official receipt will be issued by the Hon. Treasurer in all cases. Whilst it is good to reflect on the growing strength of the Junior Section, we cannot overlook that their lot is not particularly happy, having regard to the inevitable operation of the National Service (Armed Forces) Acts at a very critical stage in their athletic careers. It behoves us to keep them fully informed of club activities and events, and ensure them of an easy resettlement into club affairs on their return to civil life. The committee do not enforce the payment of club subscriptions during the period a junior member is called to service under these Acts. It is hoped, however, that junior members will notify the Hon. Secretary immediately they are called to service and keep him posted with subsequent movements. DAMAGE TO CLUB TROPHIES. In the event of a club trophy becoming damaged whilst in the safe keeping of the holder, no action should be taken regarding the repair of the trophy without prior authority of the committee. Any such action is likely to prejudice a possible claim through the club Insurance Policy. Damage to trophies, however small, and also any loss of trophy should be reported to the Hon. Treasurer immediately and a detailed statement of the casualty given. ENGRAVING OF CLUB TROPHIES. Although most holders of trophies have had my circular letter, I would here repeat as a reminder and as a guidance for future holders, that it is desirable that all trophies should be engraved up to date before the date of the next competition. Where practicable it would be appreciated if holders would arrange for the delivery of the trophy to the club engravers, The Alexander Clark Co. Ltd., 38 Leadenhall Street, E.C.3, together with the particulars of the records to be engraved; any outstanding particulars can be obtained from the Hon. Running Secretary, Mr. E. Duffett. In those cases where the records are engraved on small silver shields affixed to the trophy or to the plinth of the trophy, it will suffice if the blank small shields to be engraved are removed and posted to the engravers together with the necessary particulars to be engraved. In these cases, however, it is important that the last engraved shield should also be sent to serve as a specimen for the engraver. Where holders find this arrangement impracticable perhaps they would be good enough to arrange to let me have the trophy at a convenient date so that I can make alternative arrangements. ENGRAVING OF MEDALS. On the question of engraving of medals won by members, the last ruling given by the committee on this subject, which is still extant, is as follows: That the club undertake to engrave (1) All club medals; (2) All team race medals awarded by Athletic bodies and Associations to which the club is affiliated. BADGES, ETC. Vest badges 2/6, and Coat metal badges 2/-, are in stock. As these are sold at cost price it is requested that applications by post should be accompanied by return postage. It is regretted that there is no immediate prospect of obtaining supplies of vests and ties or other clothing. Any helpful suggestions from members on this vexed subject will be appreciated. FINALLY do not forget those subscriptions. A small item, but a very important item. You may win an award in the next club event and it would be very disappointing to find at the last moment that it was withheld because you had forgotten to pay your subscription. Be on the safe side and post it to me at once. W. G. W. W. G. W. W. G. W. Hon. Treasurer T. F. Morrell Mr. T. F. Morrell Assistant Hon. Treasurer Mr. T. F. Morrell S. Roberts Mr. S. Roberts Hon. items.sum: Running section notes: South of Thames Junior win, retention of the Pickett Cup in the Surrey County Senior Championship, coaches for the London to Brighton Relay, and summer track fixtures.
items.s: The Running Section Running section notes: South of Thames Junior win, retention of the Pickett Cup in the Surrey County Senior Championship, coaches for the London to Brighton Relay, and summer track fixtures. The results so far this season have shown our members to be carrying on the good work of last season, and although new teams have had to be found owing to the many barring clauses in some of the races, we again won the South of Thames "Junior" Race, and also supplied the first two men home. We also retained possession of the "Pickett" Cup for the Surrey County Senior Championship, although our nearest rivals, Herne Hill Harriers, put up a good show, but the forward packing of our runners turned the scales in our favour. The London to Brighton Relay is being held on April 19th, and intending supporters will be well advised to book a seat in our club coaches, which is in the hands of our Social Hon. Secretary, Dave Shepard. Track fixtures are now being made and we are hoping to hold several meetings at Tooting Common L.C.C. track, our first being on Saturday, May 17th. The previous week we have a match at the Drayton Green track with Ealing Harriers and Reading A.C. for the "Gordon Stewart" Trophy. On May 24th we have an Inter-Club match at Banstead Hospital, and members who went there last year will remember the good time, apart from the weather, that was had by all. Other fixtures, both home and away, are being arranged and it is hoped that members will do their best to support these matches, both Senior and Junior. All enquiries to the Running Hon. items.sum: Field events notes on the winter Coaching School, the S.A.A. League field events programme and a new Polytechnic Harriers multi-event competition for the Sward Trophy.
items.s: Field Events Gossip Field events notes on the winter Coaching School, the S.A.A. League field events programme and a new Polytechnic Harriers multi-event competition for the Sward Trophy. The winter field events activities have been confined to the Coaching School, which has been functioning since the beginning of November, 1946, at Belgrave Hall. Unfortunately it has not been as well supported as was anticipated, but it is hoped all who have been regularly attending will put to good use the things they have learnt when they start their summer training. With the completion of the programme the course will close, and Charlie Jones, Bill Sutton and Sid Jones will be at the Tooting Bec Track on Saturday afternoons when it is hoped the Juniors will appear and be put through their paces. The S.A.A. League (Fields Events Section) programme has just come to hand. It will be run on the same lines as last year with the exception that all events will take place on Monday evenings at the Tooting Bec Track during the months of May and June. A Junior League will also function in which Field Events will be included. In addition a Decathlon competition has been added this year for individual competitors. An interesting new competition is announced by The Polytechnic Harriers to take place at their Stadium on May 10th. The programme includes all the usual field events, three hurdle races and a steeplechase, comprising 11 events in all. The competition is both for individuals and teams. In the team competition four men score, and in this and the individual competition each competitor will be allowed to compete in not more than five selected events. Scoring will be by points from 20 points for first place to one point for 20th place. The "Sward Trophy" will be awarded to the winning team. It is hoped we can put up a very good show. T. C. J. T. items.sum: Walking section review of the winter road season, with Harry Churcher and Jack Rutland leading an unbeaten run in the open races, hopes for the National championships, Sunday strolls and new members.
items.s: With the Walkers Walking section review of the winter road season, with Harry Churcher and Jack Rutland leading an unbeaten run in the open races, hopes for the National championships, Sunday strolls and new members. Our walkers started the winter season on the road in no uncertain manner, twenty-eight members turning out for the opening Club 5 Miles Handicap. The first open, Highgate Harriers promotion, made it clear that we were making a rapid return to our pre-war predominance, at least over the shorter distances. Four in the first nine with the majority of clubs at full strength was certainly very promising. As time went on we won many other opens, Harry Churcher taking most of the individual honours with Jack Rutland a close second. As yet unbeaten, our lowest score was in the Cambridge Harriers open, when our placings were 1, 2, 3 and 5. So far there has been little opposition from the Midlands and North and presumably we shall have to wait for the new 10 miles championship to find out their present strength. One thing is certain, all the leading clubs in the country will do their utmost to become the first 10 miles champions and our succession of wins in open races will no doubt make our opponents all the more determined to prevent us from crowning our successes with National Honours. We therefore look to all concerned to see that the next few months re-establish us as the premier walking club in the country. As the National Junior Race will be over before this issue is out, little need be said, but young Mac's present form is good enough to annexe the individual title and that he will receive good support from Bert East, Harry Rouse, Joe Wilson and others. The team race on paper looks a very open affair, but once again there is not much indication of the opposition likely from the North and Midlands. With the two longer distances being held in the South, we shall not this year have the disadvantage of travelling. Although we were placed in both these races last year, with the combined efforts of all concerned, we should not be content with less than first place and a return to our pre-war position as National Champions at all distances. We have plenty of good material; all that is required is plenty of regular training, and especially for the longer distances, lots of strolling. Regarding the latter, your Road Captain, Charlie Churcher, is anxious to get a good muster for Sunday Morning strolls. With the approaching spring the weather should be more suitable for this, and it is hoped that this side of training will receive full support. The venue is Putney High Street at 9 a.m., but if you want to join in somewhere en route, get in touch with your Road Captain and he will be pleased to make the necessary arrangements. As a result of a Novices Race promoted by the M.P.A.A., two more Police members were enrolled. P. Sapcote and M. Archer, both of whom show every prospect of becoming useful walkers. George Bently, Fred's brother, back from the Forces, is with us again, and George Atkinson, also of the Police and a son of ex-Chief Inspector Atkinson, a former Barking to Southend winner, has joined us. Also Mac's young brother Sid, and Fred Herring, now first claim, will soon be available for teams. To our new members we extend a very hearty welcome and wish them many happy years with the club. Our aim is 100 active walkers, so it's up to everyone to do their bit to increase our numbers still further and thus provide some champions for the future. The Olympic Games are gradually creeping nearer. We already have men of Olympic class; these can quite easily be added to, and there is no reason why we should not produce another Olympic Champion, or perhaps even two—track and road. So good walking to you all and may our successes continue. S. R. items.sum: Junior section report on matches with Surrey A.C., Dartford Harriers and the India Cadet Company, the Surrey County Youths' and Junior Championships, and the Club Junior Cross-Country Championship for the Savage Shield won by Derrick Burfitt.
items.s: With the Juniors Junior section report on matches with Surrey A.C., Dartford Harriers and the India Cadet Company, the Surrey County Youths' and Junior Championships, and the Club Junior Cross-Country Championship for the Savage Shield won by Derrick Burfitt. On October 19th, at Wimbledon, we had a match with the junior members of Surrey A.C. and Dartford Harriers. We had the first three men home in Derrick Burfitt, Eddie Short and Arthur Bruce, who came in together, and they were followed by Len Bishop. Scoring three aside, the points were—Belgrave H. 6, Dartford H. 19, Surrey A.C. 25. In a further match of five aside between Dartford and ourselves, we won with the lower score of 25 to our visitors' 41. On November 23rd our lads made the journey to the Guards Depot, Caterham, where they were entertained to a match with the India Cadet Company. Eddie Short and Arthur Bruce came home together in first place, followed by a couple of Cadets, and then came the two Bishops brothers, Eric and Len. Next followed a whole crowd of Cadets, and eventually our other three runners, who were R. Garwood, K. E. Aspinall and B. C. Potter. The latter had lost their way and therefore their positions could not be counted in the team race. In view of the fact that we had four lads in the first six home, the Cadets very sportingly called the match a draw. Our lads then sat down to a real "Naafi" tea, and a good time was had by all! We had a team entered in the Surrey County Youths' Championship, which was held at Coulsdon on December 7th, but only managed to field four runners. Their finishing positions were—13 L. C. Bishop, 25.1; 17 E. T. Gilbert, 25.50; 39 K. E. Aspinall, 27.48; 55 L. Cheesley, 32.52. We finished sixth out of an entry of twelve teams, so our lads can be said to have done well, for with the exception of Len Bishop, this was their initial effort in on open event. The club also entered a team for the Surrey County Junior Championship, held at Earlswood on January 4th. Owing to Service calls, the age for this race being 18 to 21, we only fielded four runners, but they can be said to have done well in being beaten in the team race by the narrow margin of 2 points. Arthur Bruce ran well to finish third, with Eddie Short fourth, then Len Adams scored fifth, and Eric Bishop seventh. The course was very heavy and most of the runners had trouble in keeping their shoes on, a point to be borne in mind for future races. Finishing times of our runners were—3 A. H. Bruce, 30.24; 4 E. A. Short, 30.32; 6 L. A. Adams, 32.27; 8 E. M. Bishop, 32.50. Team scores were—S. L. H. 17 pts., Belgrave H. 19 pts. On January 18th our lads visited the Surrey A.C. at their quarters at Kingston. The match was over about 2½ miles and once again our trio of Derrick Burfitt, Eddie Short and Arthur Bruce, came home together in first place. Len Bishop duly followed in fourth place, and with the match scoring four aside, we won with the lowest possible score of 10 points to Surrey A.C.'s 26. Positions and times of our runners were—D. R. Burfitt, E. A. Short, A. H. Bruce, equal to 1st, 14 mins. 54 secs. 4 L. C. Bishop, 15.3; 6 R. Garwood, 15.21; 8 E. T. Gilbert, 15.22. The Club Junior Cross-Country Championship for the "Savage" Shield, had been postponed from December 21st owing to the frost-bound conditions, and it was now held over our usual 5 miles course on February 1st. Conditions were still far from ideal, the course being snow-covered, but a field of 8 juniors braved the conditions and are to be complimented on their fortitude. Derrick Burfitt retained his title, although Arthur Bruce ran very well to finish so close behind in second place. Eddie Short finished third, although below his usual form, and Len Bishop occupied his usual fourth place in junior events. The handicap, held in conjunction, was deservedly won by Arthur Bruce with R. Garwood taking second award and Eddie Short the third prize. Positions and times are given below:— E. A. D. items.s: 5 Miles C.C. Handicap Report and result of the club 5 Miles Cross-Country Handicap and match with Surrey A.C. at Wimbledon on 26 October 1946, scratch race won by Dick Towndrow and handicap by Vic Blowfield. 5 MILES C.C. HANDICAP SATURDAY, OCTOBER 26th, 1946, WIMBLEDON Held at Wimbledon on October 26th, and once again a very large field was seen out. We had a match with Surrey A.C. in conjunction with this race, and were pleased to welcome many old friends. Dick Towndrow, making one of his rare appearances in our colours, was a good winner of the scratch race, followed by Vic Blowfield, who in his first attempt at cross-country racing, certainly surprised many by his forward running. Stan Belton, of Surrey A.C., came along with Len Herbert, and they appeared to be taking things fairly steady, as is wise so early in the season. The Club Handicap was won by Vic Blowfield, who made good use of the Handicapper's generosity. Len Bishop, one of our promising junior members, came second, with Les Stokell, another newcomer to our ranks, taking third award. We were pleased to see Bert Footer and Arthur Penny, the famous Belgrave "twins," making a return to active racing again, and look forward to their help throughout the season. Scoring six aside in the match with Surrey A.C., we won the team contest by scoring 29 points to Surrey's 49. Result of 5 Miles Handicap * Dead heat Position Name Act. Time Start Hcp. items.s: Match v. Finchley Harriers Report of a heavy-going cross-country match with Finchley Harriers at Ruislip on 23 November, won by Belgrave 224½ points to 240½. On November 23rd we visited Ruislip for a match with the Finchley Harriers. The course was in a very bad state, being almost water-logged throughout, and for some of our members it was a most gruelling race. Finchley had the first two men home and then came Derrick Burfitt, who made light of the conditions, although losing a shoe, and having to catch up on his field again. Scoring 15 aside, we won the match with 224½ points to Finchley's 240½, but all the runners are to be complimented on finishing such a sticky course. Placings of our runners were—D. R. Burfitt 3, T. items.s: South of Thames "Junior" Race Report of the South of Thames Junior cross-country race at Nonsuch Park, Cheam, on 9 November, won by Bill Lucas with Belgrave "A" retaining the team title from Herne Hill. Held at Non-Such Park, Cheam, on November 9th, a field of 209 runners, representing 29 teams, fought out a closely-contested race over a two-lap course. As winners of the race last season, we thus had to find a new scoring team, and our hopes received a set-back when Vic Blowfield failed to arrive in time. However, at the half-way stage in the race, Bill Lucas and Len Marchant were in the leading bunch of four runners, which was a good start-off to our team's chances. When they came in sight of the finish Bill Lucas was clear away in front and in second position came Len Marchant, a fine performance by both runners. Herne Hill had three runners finish in a bunch and the team result was in doubt until the discs had been checked over. It was then found that we totalled 41 points to Herne Hill's 48, and we had thus repeated our victory of last year in this event. Finishing positions and times of our runners were:— 1 W. E. Thames Valley Harriers Report of a four-cornered cross-country match at Cranford on 7 December with Thames Valley Harriers, Surrey A.C. and Metropolitan Police A.C., won by Thames Valley with Belgrave second. Held at Cranford on December 7th, and a good crowd of our members were present. Other clubs competing in a four-cornered match were Surrey A.C. and Metropolitan Police A.C. Once again the course was very muddy but Stan Belton of Surrey, revelled in the conditions to come home a good winner. Vic Blowfield ran excellently to finish second, and continues to show great promise in his first season over the country. Scoring six aside in the four-club match, resulted thus—Thames Valley H. 45 points, Belgrave H. 59, Surrey A.C. 114, Metropolitan Police 256. There was also a 16 aside match between Thames Valley and ourselves, and the home club won with 326 points to our 329. Placings of our runners were:— V. S. Blowfield 2, G. M. Pearson 7, T. G. items.sum: Report and result of the Club Seven Miles Cross-Country Championship at Wimbledon on 14 December 1946, won by Len Herbert from Vic Blowfield, with handicap placings.
items.s: Club Seven Miles C.C. Championship Report and result of the Club Seven Miles Cross-Country Championship at Wimbledon on 14 December 1946, won by Len Herbert from Vic Blowfield, with handicap placings. CLUB SEVEN MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP SATURDAY, DECEMBER 14th, 1946, WIMBLEDON The day was mild, but the fog which had hung over London for two previous days was still covering the common. The President started a field of 30 runners, a total nearly up to pre-war standards. Dick Tobin lead the field out at a fair pace, then bunched together were Carter, Bill Lucas, Clinton, Abberton, Eales, Blowfield, Penny, with Footer and Morrell a little behind, and Len Herbert at the rear. The race was next seen at the Windmill on the first lap. Here the field was beginning to shake itself out, Tom Carter was leading a group consisting of Clinton, Abberton, Penny, Blowfield and Herbert, but it was still anybody's race. This order was kept at the turn on to the second lap, albeit Footer was coming up to the leaders and was obviously running his usual "snaky" race. By now the Common was turning dark and very foggy, and it was obvious the race would finish in darkness. Over the last two miles or so Herbert went away in fine style to win from Vic Blowfield with Frank Abberton a strong third. These three were followed closely by Tom Carter and Bert Footer, Bert managing to beat Tom in a sprint down the finishing straight. Congratulations must go to Len Herbert on his first C.C. Club Championship and to Vic Blowfield and Frank Abberton on their improved running. Also to Bert Footer and Arthur Penny on their "comebacks." Result of 7 Miles C.C. items.s: Club Boxing Day Meeting Report and results of the club's Boxing Day track meeting at Tooting Common track, with the 100 yards handicap won by A. D. Sexton and the 2 miles by L. M. Marchant. Our annual track meeting was held on Boxing Day morning at Tooting Common track, and a large crowd was present to witness some good racing. In the 100 Yards Sprint Handicap there were six heats, although owing to absentees, some were sparsely filled. Heat winners were—D. Cook (8 yds.), A. C. Allen (8½ yds.), A. D. Sexton (5 yds.), R. C. Negus (5 yds.), J. Heathfield (7½ yds.) and E. M. Bishop (8½ yds.). The final was a closely-contested race between three of our junior members, and Alan Sexton just beat Dick Negus, with D. Cook third. In the 2 Miles Run, Derrick Burfitt, the A.A.A. junior mile champion, was on the virtual scratch mark of 20 yards. He ran an excellent race to work his way through the field, and although Vic Blowfield hung closely on his heels, Derrick finished a good second to Len Marchant, the winner, with a yard or two to spare from Vic Blowfield, who was third. 100 Yards Handicap—1 A. items.s: The County Championships Reports of Belgrave members in the Surrey, Middlesex, Kent and Hertfordshire county cross-country championships, including Belgrave's Surrey team title and Derrick Burfitt's fourth successive junior win. SURREY. The Surrey County Senior Cross-Country Championship was held over 7 miles of heavy country at Earlswood, on January 4th. Stan Belton, of Surrey A.C., soon went into the lead, and although Len Herbert, making his usual slow start, gradually overhauled his field, he could not catch Belton, who won in good style. Frank Abberton displayed fine form in gaining third place, and as he has now joined us first-claim, he should prove an asset to our teams. Bill Lucas ran in his usual excellent style to finish 4th, and Les Stokell, in his first season over the country, put up a fine performance to gain sixth place, and so gain his County colours. Tom Carter, although below his usual form, nevertheless ran a plucky race to gain twelfth position and split a couple of Herne Hill runners up the finishing straight to do so. Bert Mitchell was the sixth scoring member of our team in nineteenth place, and our thanks go to Jimmy Wood, our second-claim member, for helping Bert along. Other members of our team finished—21 Eric Herbert, 23 Tom Morrell, 25 Stan Eales, 32 Syd Jarlett, 39 Con Abberton, 42 Gordon Doubleday. The team championship resulted—1 Belgrave Harriers 45 points; 2 Herne Hill H. 74 points; 3 Surrey A.C. 101 points. MIDDLESEX. Our members in this race were representing Cadogan A.C., the holders of the title, but they sadly missed Dave Main, Dan Patience and Charlie Smart, and had to take third place in the team championship. Our members' positions and times were—8 G. M. Pearson, 53.5; 11 R. W. Tobin, 53.45; 23 K. G. Stimpson, 55.16; 32 H. W. Shields, 56.12; 37 A. E. Taylor, 57.4; 41 T. G. Clinton, 57.36; 46 A. Smith, 58.17; 59 C. Mains, 59.56. Derrick Burfitt retained his hold on the Junior title, which he won in 34 mins. 18 secs., and this makes his fourth successive win, which must be a record which will last for all time. KENT. George Lucas ran as an individual in his County Championship, and did well to finish in sixth place, thus gaining his County Colours. HERTS. A. E. Frost, our Civil Service member, ran in this race and finished fourth, and is now displaying a return to his pre-war form. items.s: Inter-Counties' Championship Report of Belgrave members running for Surrey, Middlesex, Kent and Hertfordshire in the Inter-Counties cross-country championship at Nottingham on 18 January, with Vic Blowfield sixth. This race was held at Nottingham on January 18th, and there were quite a number of Belgrave members representing their Counties. Tom Carter had made the journey as captain of the Surrey team, which also included Frank Abberton, Len Herbert, Bill Lucas and Les Stokell. Running for Middlesex were Vic Blowfield, who had dropped out of the County race owing to shoe trouble, and Geoff Pearson, while George Lucas was in Kent colours, and A. E. Frost was running for Hertfordshire. Our congratulations go to all these runners for the honour conferred upon them in representing their County, and Vic Blowfield is to be complimented on his fine showing in such company. To finish sixth only six seconds behind the winner was a fine performance and further honours should certainly come his way. George Lucas also did well in finishing thirteenth and helping his County to win the team championship. Frank Abberton was sixteenth, Len Herbert thirty-sixth, Bill Lucas forty-third, Les Stokell forty-fifth, Geoff Pearson sixtieth, and A. E. Frost ninety-fifth. Championship Report and result of the Club Ten Miles Cross-Country Championship on 25 January 1947, won by Vic Blowfield for the Macher Shield, with Albert Frost first on handicap; as printed, two handicap times do not equal actual time less start: V. S. Blowfield 58.45 (59.58 less 1.15 = 58.43, and the same 58.45 as A. H. Bishop, placed 9th) and B. Olver 70.15 (74.45 less 5.30 = 69.15). CLUB TEN MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP SATURDAY, JANUARY 25th, 1947 A very cold day greeted the small field for this race. Owing to sickness there were many notable absentees including both the Herbert's, both the Lucas's and Frank Abberton. The field was led out by Tom Carter but was well together when at 2 miles Carter went into the lead. Tom's lead, however, was doomed as his injured leg gave way immediately and he had to retire from the race. At the halfway stage Arthur Penny and Vic Blowfield were running together with the rest of the field strung out in this order—Pearson, Frost, Eales, Tobin, Stokell. Here Tommy Morrell, looking beat, retired, and Tom Clinton, well off form, was seen running well to the rear. Over the last three miles Blowfield moved away from Penny to win well and strongly. Thus at his first attempt Vic won the Macher Shield. His running this season being consistently good and improving, he certainly deserved the honour. Arthur Penny also showed some of his old form in giving Vic such a stiff race, his comeback is a magnificent one. Albert Frost and Stan Eales showed welcome returns to form and took the first and second handicap prizes. Position Name Act. Time Start Hcp. Time Postn. in Hcp. 1 V. S. Our entry of four teams (29 individuals) was second only to that of the promoting club. Harry Churcher, going over the course for the first time, found it necessary to keep with Jack Rutland the greater part of the way. After a slow start up a very trying hill, these two soon got to the front of the field and thereafter maintained their lead throughout until the last few yards, when Harry just managed to finish 1 second in front of Jack. Backed up by McMullen (4th) and Joe Coleman (9th), we scored a fairly easy win with 16 points, the promoting club being 2nd with 24 points. A. East, who had been showing such good form, offended the judges about half-a-mile from home and was ruled out. Of 20 teams our "B" team was 8th and "C" team 9th. Belgrave placings:— 1 H. items.s: Belgrave Open Walk Report and Belgrave placings in the club's own open walk on 30 November 1946, with 158 starters, won by Jack Rutland after Harry Churcher was ruled out, Belgrave winning the team race from Woodford Green and Leicester Walking Club, with thanks to prize-fund donors. BELGRAVE OPEN WALK NOVEMBER 30th, 1946 Our own open did not attract quite as large an entry as had been anticipated, but of the 176 entries 158 started on a signal from the Club President. Harry Churcher contented himself with accompanying C. Morris of the Surrey A.C. for the first lap, after which he began to make a lead. Jack Rutland, on returning to the common, then went up into second place, and with McMullen, Joe Coleman, Len Fletcher and Bob Readman not far behind it soon became apparent that, barring a number of accidents, we should add one more to our list of successes. Harry continued to walk in excellent style until about half-a-mile from home when, to the surprise of everyone, he was ruled out, leaving Jack Rutland in the lead. This unfortunate occurrence gave Len Fletcher, competing in his first open for a considerable time, an opportunity of sharing in the team honours. Despite Harry's misfortune we won easily from Woodford Green by 21 points to 55 points, with Leicester Walking Club third with 57 points. From the result of the Enfield Open it was evident that competition between the "A" and "B" teams for handicap awards would be very keen. This proved even closer than was anticipated and resulted in the "A" team taking first place with the "B" team 1 second behind. Colin Sutton, starting from a longer mark than Len Fletcher found his way into the winning handicap team at Len's expense. Joe Scamell took the Veterans' prize, and Bob Readman the special prize for the first club member not gaining any other award. The account would be incomplete without recording our most sincere thanks to the following for their donations to the prize fund:—Messrs. H. Evans, J. Bellchamber, A. A. Harley, A. Harley (Senr.), A. Beales, P. Wright, C. Sutton, F. Elson, C. Churcher, H. Churcher, J. Crump and F. Thompson. Also to Mrs. Churcher for presenting a special prize. Lastly we are indebted to the R.W.A. MATCH v. HIGHGATE HARRIERS DECEMBER 28th, 1946, at PARLIAMENT HILL Our return match with Highgate being on almost the shortest day of the year was reduced to 5½ miles. Despite the close proximity to Christmas, 12 of our walkers turned out to tackle the hilly course, to our opponents 15, both sides had most of their best men out. Although Jack Rutland set a hot pace at the start and gained a lead of about 40 yards, after 2 miles he went slightly off the course. This gave Harry Churcher the chance to catch up with him and after a neck and neck race, Harry eventually took the lead to win by 23 seconds. CLUB 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP JANUARY 25th, 1947 MURPHY SHIELD Twenty walkers, including Alf Pope, 2nd claim, turned out for the Club 10 miles championship and handicap, and a match versus the Police made an added interest. Dick Murphy was there to start the race and also presented the awards at the conclusion. The cold weather and the additional distance, after sevens, seemed to affect many of the walkers, and apart from Harry Churcher times were not very good. Jack Rutland suffered with leg trouble during the later stages of the race and dropped back into 3rd position. Don Heath, walking slightly above his usual form, scored another handicap win, with Capt. Charlie 2nd and Joe Wilson 3rd. The match resulted in a win for the club by 93 points to 160. 1 H. items.label: No. 102
items.sum: Editorial apologising for the long gap since the last issue and, in the club's Diamond Jubilee year, urging members to remember the work behind Belgrave's success and to volunteer as officials.
items.s: Editorial Editorial apologising for the long gap since the last issue and, in the club's Diamond Jubilee year, urging members to remember the work behind Belgrave's success and to volunteer as officials. It has been a long time since the last issue. Your Hon. Editor must take some of the blame for this lapse. He apologises and hopes you will accept his excuses of too much work and, therefore, too little leisure in which to produce this journal. The rest of the blame must fall on that well-known scapegoat, “ circumstances beyond our control,” and on those few contributors who were tardy in sending their material. This is Belgrave's Diamond Jubilee year. Sixty years is a long time for a Club such as ours to have been in existence. It has seen two most terrible World Wars and it has lost some of its best sons in each. But now in this Year of our Lord, 1947, it is flourishing, winning and expanding like no other club in England to-day. Those of us who know Belgrave know the reason for this happy state of affairs. And we also know that we are not just enjoying one of those cycles of success but that the youth of the Club is pressing towards the day when it can burst into its own. One had only to observe, this summer, the members performing in the “ under sixteen ” events to see furthermore that we have a second layer of younger members already keen and already infused with the Belgrave spirit. Very satisfying all of this, but we must not become too smug, we must not accept our success as falling from the heavens to us. Remember, that it took hard work to build the Club. Hard work raising every penny of its money, hard work making runners, walkers, throwers, hard work organising, hard work enlarging the membership, and all of this must have often seemed at the time nothing but “ sweat, tears and blood.” We are now reaping our sowings. But let us remember, that it still means sowing, and to sow is to labour. The older members who helped to turn this Club into such a glorious one will not forget that which has passed. The younger members, knowing only the fullness of the Club, might be tempted to forget and take too much for granted at times unless they always carry in their minds a knowledge of the labour accomplished for their benefit and for the glory of the Club. So that a Club of Belgrave's size and importance should function efficiently a great deal of work is still being done by its officials. These people, the president, secretaries, treasurer, captains and vice-captains, elected committee, and many other volunteers and helpers, give up most of their spare time for the Club's good. We are always in need of good officials and willing helpers. So let anybody who thinks he can be of use in this way not hide his light under a bushel. We need you!

items.sum: Commentary column of club news: Frank Elson's recovery, Charles Smart's running in Germany, new member Bert Ellsey, members elected to S.C.C.C.A. and R.W.A. committees, Alf Harley's offices, Alf Taylor's return, Dick Towndrow joining, and social dates.
items.s: Commentary Commentary column of club news: Frank Elson's recovery, Charles Smart's running in Germany, new member Bert Ellsey, members elected to S.C.C.C.A. and R.W.A. committees, Alf Harley's offices, Alf Taylor's return, Dick Towndrow joining, and social dates. Mention of members' athletic feats are not being made in the Commentary for this issue. This is mainly because there have been so many of them that space would hardly permit. Such mentions are made elsewhere in this journal. It is, however, our aim to produce “ The Belgravian ” quarterly in the future and therefore enable this Commentary to cover its traditional wide range again. Frank Elson is now out of hospital and has been seen training at the Duke of York's. We are all most happy to see Frank making such a recovery, and we hope it will continue. Charles Smart, writing from Germany, tells of some fast running, including a win he accomplished in a half-an-hour's race. He missed the six mile mark by a mere 220 yards or so, and that on a wet, gusty day! Bert Ellsey, who has recently joined us, is one of the old school of cross-country runners, having graduated with the now defunct Boro Poly A.C. and Ashcombe St. Georges. He was always a good team man and should be a useful addition to our list of officials. He is a vice-president of the English Cross-Country Union, is past-president of the Southern Counties C.C.A., vice-president and vice-chairman of the Surrey County A.A.A., president of the South of Thames C.C.A. and has a seat on the Southern Committee of the A.A.A. Harry Shields has been re-elected to the committee of the Southern Counties C.C.A. Harry will, no doubt, raise a shout for us here! Joe Coleman, Charles Churcher and Harry Rouse have been elected to the Southern Committee of the R.W.A. Our hon. secretary, Alf Harley, is organising the Olympic Road Walk. Besides this, Alf is hon. treasurer of the R.W.A., vice-president of the Southern Committee of the R.W.A. and R.W.A. delegate to the A.A.A. Alf Taylor has come through an operation and is now running again. One of our best runners of the past, it is good to see Alf out again. Dick Towndrow has now joined us as a first claim member. Our Social Hon. Secretary sends these dates for Belgrave Socials at Belgrave Hall; 15th November, 13th December, Special Xmas Party 27th December, 24th January, 1948. items.label: No. 102
items.sum: Walking notes on the 1947 road and track season: championships, opens, matches and club races, with Harry Churcher's A.A.A. and Irish-record successes and the double win in the new 10 miles National.
items.s: Walking News and Results Walking notes on the 1947 road and track season: championships, opens, matches and club races, with Harry Churcher's A.A.A. and Irish-record successes and the double win in the new 10 miles National. Following the splendid progress made by our walkers as reported in our last issue, the road season continued with still further successes. Although the Junior team at Leicester could get no better than 4th place, all our men walked up to expectations. The only disappointment being the loss of the individual title which we had hoped would be annexed by young Mac. Brown of Enfield, however, struck some excellent form and Mac had to be content with second place. Team honours went to our old friends Surrey Walking Club rapidly returning to strength and to say the least, the Championship has come back to the home county. High light of the season was the double win in the new 10 miles National Championship. Following a succession of wins in open road races over a similar distance, everyone looked forward to the Bels giving a good account of themselves. With our scoring four in the first six and an aggregate of 13 points, it should be many years before this record is equalled, let alone beaten. Jack Rutland's performance is particularly worthy of mention, since we had begun to feel that his best distance was 7 miles. A week later the new National Road Champion gained still further honours by annexing once more the A.A.A. title on the track at 7 miles. Harry led all the way round maintaining an almost even lap schedule, to win comfortably from the two Italians, one of whom made a bold attempt to overtake him in the last three miles. Our remaining men, all walked exceedingly well and were successful in gaining standards. The Club 20 proved a very interesting race. 26 competitors faced the starter, our old friend Dick Murphy, and as it was already known that a few intended using it only as a training spin, it was not surprising that only 16 finished. Right from the start our Road Captain, Charlie Churcher set the pace, followed by Joe Coleman. Colin Sutton, walking very wisely, kept well back in the early stages, but eventually made up quite a lot of ground and although he was unable to seriously challenge Charlie for the lead, eventually finished an easy second. Joe Coleman dropped back in the later stages of the raec allowing Bob Readman to take the third position. Jack Rutland had previously stated that he intended to retire early in the race owing to a bad cold the week before, and judging by the race in general, we had every hope of making our presence felt in the National 20 a fortnight later. Fate, however, was unkind to us at the last minute, as we received news that Colin Sutton was in bed with bronchitis. Coupled with Joe Coleman's retirement from the race at 8 miles with cramp, our chances were considerably weakened. I will not say any more except to say that all our walkers gave an excellent account of themselves and to congratulate our old friends Surrey Walking Club on their fine win. The Inter-Club Contest at Tooting Bec Common proved a great improvement on last year. Entries were received from eight clubs, but unfortunately only ourselves and Surrey W.C. were able to turn out a full team of eight. The contest, therefore, developed into a battle between us and Surrey W.C. in which we came out top. Harry Churcher had a great duel with Jim Morris (S.A.C.) in the four miles and eventually took the lead and won, giving us a good start. Our lads filled first place in all the four events At Motspur Park on June 7th, Harry Churcher once again showed the way home in the Surrey County Championship, with Mac and Joe Coleman filling second and third places. Three weeks later they repeated the process in the Southern Counties Championships, finishing in the same order. Earlier in the day Jack Rutland had secured the new County Title—7 miles—showing Eddie Staker of Highgate a clean pair of heels. Successes have followed one on top of another, both individual and team. Despite the fact that Harry Churcher was not entered for the two miles team race at the Kinnaird Meeting—he should have been in France but the trip was cancelled at the last minute—our lads, led by Mac, won with an aggregate of 13 points. In the 10,000 metres events, Harry once again gave a grand exhibition of walking. At Tooting on 25th June, Jim Morris again gave him a good race, but was unable to get the better of him. On this occasion Harry returned the excellent time of 46.27. Congratulations to Gordon Doubleday on his admission to that very select fraternity “ The Centurions,” which he achieved in the Brighton and Back on June 20-21st. Fred Herring, unfortunately, had to retire at 30 miles, but no doubt he will have another shot. In the R.W.A. 50 kilos at Eastleigh we again met with misfortune. Both Charlie Churcher and Jack Bidgood were compelled to retire owing to bad blisters, at a time when we had a good opportunity of being placed, so once again we must congratulate our friends of the Surrey Walking Club on their fine win. The long distance races this season have made it clear that we need some more good distance men. Next year we hope to have the services of Bert Webb. Jack Baker is showing great improvement, as also is Sapcote, who, unfortunately, was on the Sick List and unable to compete. Bob Readman too, was absent, having arrested a couple of housebreakers, so we must be content to make a real effort during the coming season to build up a really strong team capable of bringing back to the club the National titles we held before the war. There were eight entries for the Novices 1 mile race at Tooting Bec on 9th July. Maynard, a new club member, walked in fine style to win, followed by two of our Police friends, Tasker and Noonan, both of whom we hope will soon be members of the Club. Jimmy Coates, our youngest active walker, showed considerable improvement and finished fourth. Harry Churcher's visit to Dublin on 9-7-47 with the A.A.A. team proved most successful, his time 21.23 for the three miles being a new Irish record, the previous best, 22.8, having stood since 1919. In the A.A.A. two miles at White City on July 19th, he once again put up a very fast time of 13.56 only to be beaten by the holder, Hindmar by the very small margin of two seconds. To sum up the activities of the Walkers during the past few months it may be said that everyone has given of his best, and although that best wasn't always quite good enough, the name of Belgrave stands to-day as prominent in walking circles as ever. items.h: SOUTH OF THAMES 7 MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP
items.sum: South of Thames 7 miles cross-country championship in snow at Windsor Great Park, where Belgrave were second to Aylesford P.M. with a record low second-place score and won the Colman Cup.
e: South of Thames Cross Country Championships
items.s: SOUTH OF THAMES 7 MILES C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP South of Thames 7 miles cross-country championship in snow at Windsor Great Park, where Belgrave were second to Aylesford P.M. with a record low second-place score and won the Colman Cup. RUNNING NEWS AND RESULTS This race was held in Windsor Great Park, and the course was snow-covered and badly frozen in places. A field of 176 runners comprising 20 teams faced the starter, and owing to the way the course was situated, the runners disappeared from sight up the Long Walk towards the “ Copper Horse ” and one only saw them again when they came in sight on the homward stretch. George Lucas ran a fine race to finish 5th while Les Stokell in finishing 7th justified our high hopes of him as a real “ find.” Albert Frost also ran well to finish 9th and with Bill Lucas 14th, Stan Eales 24th and Syd Jarlett 28th, our team scored 87 points, a total that in most years would have won the team championship, and is actually the lowest score ever recorded by a team taking second place. Eric Herbert was unlucky to miss a medal by one place, while our team of 12 won the “ Colman ” Cup, which is awarded to the club with the lowest score for its team of 12 men to finish. Norman Walker is to be thanked for this, as he only turned up to watch but was pressed into service with “ borrowed ” togs in order for us to field a complete team. items.s: SOUTHERN SENIOR C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP Southern senior cross-country championship at Ascot, won by Len Herbert, with Belgrave second to Aylesford P.M. by 5 points. The race was held after the Junior event on Ascot Racecourse, so that a fairly clear trail had been made in the snow, and from the start Olney of T.V.H. set a fast pace. Stan Belton and Len Herbert kept with him throughout and although the former was dropped over the last two hundred yards, Herbert only got by Olney down the finishing straight. Our friends from Aylesford repeated their South of Thames victory over us, although we were without Les Stokell, resting an injured ankle, while George Lucas had an off-day. Even so, they only won by the narrow margin of 5 points, and Vic Blowfield and Albert Frost again ran extremely well. We were also the holders of the “ Odling-Smee ” Cup, awarded to the first club to finish their team of 12 men, but owing to Bert Footer's retirement, only had 11 in the first 93 places, there actually being 244 finishers. items.s: T.V.H. ROAD RELAY RACE T.V.H. road relay won by Belgrave's A team from Birchfield Harriers, Len Herbert outsprinting Bobby Reid on the last leg. There was an entry of 22 teams for this annual event, and once again our Midland rivals, the Birchfield Harriers, travelled down to compete. Owing to the uncertainty of George Lucas's leg trouble we had decided to let him run the first leg for our “ C ” team, and nobody was very much surprised when he came home with the lead. Albert Frost then took our “ A ” team into the lead, which Vic Blowfield kept, although going slightly off the course, which enabled the Birchfield man to get close on his heels. Len Herbert went off just in front of Bobby Reid for the final leg, and they turned the last corner still together, but Len got in front with a fine finishing burst. Our “ B ” team had also run well to gain 4th place, and only a record-breaking run by Alec Olney deprived them of third place. The “ C ” team fifinished 6th, and our “ D ” team 11th, which considering the entry was a very good performance on all our lads' part. items.label: No. 102
items.sum: Review of Belgrave's 1947 Diamond Jubilee track season: poor turnouts for matches, and the leading individuals including Willie Nankeville.
items.s: THE TRACK SEASON Review of Belgrave's 1947 Diamond Jubilee track season: poor turnouts for matches, and the leading individuals including Willie Nankeville. Although 1947 was our Diamond Jubilee season, the season taken as a whole, was rather disappointing from the general point of view. We did moderately well in club matches, although so long as our members receive competition, the actual results do not matter so much. What is more important, is the support given these fixtures by club members and both Harry Shields and Frank Webb were far from satisfified with the results of their numerous cards to members asking them to turn up for the various matches. Another disappointing feature was the lack of support for the open team and relay events for which the club entered teams and then had to withdraw owing to insufficient numbers being present. This raises the question of whether a Team and Relay Secretary should be appointed, and I am sure our Committee would welcome any volunteers for this onerous position. Individually, we had our members well to the fore in the various championships and representative matches, and outstanding was Willie Nankeville, the first Englishman to finish in a record-breaking 1 mile race at the A.A.A. championships. Willie also represented his country in the match v. France in Paris, and looks a certain choice for the Olympic Games 1,500 metres. Len Marchant, George Lucas and Len Herbert also represented the A.A.A. during the season, and J. T. Cope and W. W. Lockyer gave promise of better things to come and should both be troubling the best next season. Our young South African member, E. N. McKenzie, also showed up well during the season and stands a very good chance of representing his country at next year's Olympic Games. Derrick Burfitt found his R.A.F. duties against record-breaking performances, which has been his wont in the past, but even so he turned out for the club whenever he was home on leave and we much appreciated his help. The club handicaps were also not so well supported as we have been used to in pre-war years, when we were at Battersea Park, and we may have to prune these for next season. items.s: MATCH v. EALING HARRIERS Three-sided match at Drayton Green on 10 May in which Belgrave beat Walton A.C. and Ealing Harriers to keep the Gordon Stewart Trophy. This was held at the Drayton Green track on May 10th, and took the form of a three-sided match for the “ Gordon Stewart ” Trophy, last competed for in 1939. Clubs competing were Ealing Harriers, Walton A.C., and ourselves, and the final scores were—Belgrave H. 30 points. Walton A.C. 24 points. Ealing H. 10 points. Our Canadian sprinter, Al Page, turned out for us, prior to returning to Canada, and ran well to finish second in the 100 to Lewis of Walton, and also gained third place in the 220 yards. Bill Lucas won the 1 mile, and Len Marchant ran away with the 880 with Vic Blowfield in second place. Our 2 milers suffered a shock when Turing of Walton went away in the final lap to win in 10 mins. dead. We won the final event, the 1 mile Medley relay and so retained our hold on the trophy, and express our thanks to the local club for a pleasant afternoon's sport. items.s: INTER-CLUB MATCH AT BANSTEAD Ten-club inter-club match at Banstead Hospital grounds on 24 May, which Belgrave won ahead of South London Harriers to become first holders of a new trophy. This was held in the Hospital grounds on May 24th, and our old member Alec Robertshaw was in charge of the ground arrangements, and this year the weather was much kinder than last. Ten clubs had been invited to compete for a brand new trophy to be awarded annually, and we were very pleased to become the first holders of the trophy. It was a neck-and-neck struggle between South London Harriers and ourselves throughout, and our members can be said to have done well against such opposition. Ted Read ran second to Liffen of S.L.H. in the 100, while Jack Frost was second in the first strings 220 yards, and E. N. McKenzie displayed impressive form in winning the second strings race. Stan Botwright and Fred Clay, a welcome visitor, gained us further points in the two 440 yards races, and Len Marchant won the 880 yards in fine style for so early in the season. Vic Blowfield and Derrick Burfitt also picked up useful points in the 1 mile event, and our team also won the team race in the 2 miles race. Willie Nankeville turned out in the 1 mile medley relay and led our team to a fine victory. Final team scores were—Belgrave H. 65. South London H. 53. Surrey A.C. 29. Finchley H. 29. Mitcham A.C. 28. e: Match v. Dorking St. Paul's A.C.
items.s: MATCH v. DORKING ST. PAUL'S A.C. Triangular match at Dorking St. Paul's A.C. with Worthing and District, which Belgrave lost by one point. Held at the local club's ground with the lovely Box Hill in the background, this was also a triangular match, with Worthing and District making the long journey from the coast in order to compete. The match was rightly started prompt on time, but we were then very short of numbers, although our members turned up in good strength later in the afternoon. Les Christmas ran in the 100 yards and did well to gain second place, while for the next event the 880 yards, we had Ben Lulham and Freddie Bradnum, and Lulham gained second place in a slow run race. For the 440 yards we had Jack Frost and Jim Beaumont taking first two places, while Bill Lucas won the 1 mile in 4 min. 34.3 secs., with Frank Abberton in third place. Incidentally we turned out, with the home club's permission, about a dozen runners, as several of our distance runners had turned up under the impression that a 2 miles was on the programme, and rather than disappoint them, it was agreed to let them all run in the 1 mile event. Ted Read and Les Christmas were first and second in the 220 yards, and we also won the medley relay race. Final scores saw us lose the match by the narrow margin of one point, we scored 46 to the home club's 47, with Worthing scoring 37. After the meeting we were entertained to tea in the club pavilion and all agreed it was a good afternoon out in the country, and we look forward to next season's return fixture. items.sum: Belgrave performances at the 1947 A.A.A. championships, including Willie Nankeville third in the record-breaking mile and George Lucas third in the 3 miles.
items.s: A.A.A. CHAMPIONSHIPS Belgrave performances at the 1947 A.A.A. championships, including Willie Nankeville third in the record-breaking mile and George Lucas third in the 3 miles. We had quite a good entry for these championships, and our men put up a most creditable show and enhanced the club's name by so doing. Len Marchant qualified for the final of the 880 yards and Willie Nankeville did likewise in the 1 mile event. Charlie Smart, on leave from Germany, where he is with the Control Commission, ran an excellent race in the 6 miles event, and although short of distance training, he finished a good third to Chivers (Reading) and Peters, the holder. On the Saturday, Harry Churcher set the pace by a thrilling race in the 2 miles walk, and then Willie Nankeville set us roaring by making the pace in the 1 mile final, and he eventually finished third to Garay (Hungary), and Slykhuis (Holland), in the record time, for this event, of 4 min. 10.6 secs. Len Marchant, although running well in the 880 final, had to be content with fifth place in a fast run race. In the 3 miles, George Lucas ran well to gain third place behind Lataster (Holland) and Olney (T.V.H.), while after a slow start, Len Herbert ran through to finish sixth. Len is convinced that these tactics suit him best, but in such company we still remain to be assured that anyone, apart from a Wally Beavers, can catch his field and go through to win. A repetition of this year's form in next season's championships should ensure us of representation in Britain's team for the Olympic Games, and we have several “ dark horses ” yet to show their paces in these championships. This was held on July 23rd, and our opponents were Herne Hill H. and Dorking St. Paul's A.C. Both the latter club and ourselves were poorly represented and as Herne Hill had Wilkinson and Higgins for the short sprints, they naturally scored major points in both these events. Len Marchant won the 880 in 1 min. 59.2 secs. and E. N. McKenzie was second, while Syd Jarlett and Bob Wise were second and third in the 440 yards. Charlie Smart turned out for us in the 1 mile and did well to finish third to Rowe and J. H. Barry, the Irish runner now with Herne Hill. items.sum: Report of Belgrave's track match against Thames Valley Harriers (and Southgate Harriers) at Alperton on 26 July 1947, lost to T.V.H.
items.s: MATCH v. THAMES VALLEY HARRIERS Report of Belgrave's track match against Thames Valley Harriers (and Southgate Harriers) at Alperton on 26 July 1947, lost to T.V.H. MATCH v. THAMES VALLEY HARRIERS Held at Alperton Track on July 26th, and our numbers were on the small side, but those members who did turn up had an enjoyable afternoon's sport. Those who were privileged to witness Dave Martin-Shepherd's efforts in the Long Jump will not readily forget his style of jumping, it had to be seen to be believed! However, we do thank him for turning out at short notice and we were also pleased to see Derrick Burfitt present although he only arrived home on leave that same morning. Once again we were short of sprinters and failed to score a point in these events. E. N. McKenzie won the 880 yards in impressive style in 2 min. 1 sec., and Derrick Burfitt ran away from his opponents in the 1 mile to return 4 min. 31 secs. V. D. Wynyard was third in the 440 and Tom Clinton ran in good style to win the 2 miles event. We had to make up a scratch team for the medley relay, but even so Derrick Burfitt almost caught Anzola of T.V.H. over the final stage. I almost forgot to mention that Southgate Harriers were also competing although their numbers were even smaller than our own. Final scores were — Thames Valley H. 53. Belgrave H. 35. Southgate H. 19. items.s: THE CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS Report and full results of the Belgrave Harriers club track championships at Tooting on 2 August 1947, with standard medal winners. THE CLUB CHAMPIONSHIPS Held at Tooting Track on August 2nd, before a large crowd, and some good racing was seen. Ted Read retained his 100 yards title, with a newcomer in G. R. Lowers in second place. Alan Sexton beat D. J. Merrett in the 100 yards Junior, and repeated this performance in the 220 yards junior event. The 100 yards Boys race saw D. E. Marshall beat a fellow school-mate in R. M. Davis, with M. Baker third. The expected dust-up between Len Marchant and E. N. McKenzie saw Len an easy winner at the finish, as “ Mac ” made his effort too soon and finished a very tired young man. Arthur Bruce won the Junior 880 with Len Bishop second and B. Arnold third, and it is interesting to note that all these three lads are in the Services. M. Paxton who is actually a junior, ran in the 440 yards and won his heat in good style. In the final J. T. Cope and Jack Frost, the holder, had a neck-and-neck struggle with Cope getting the verdict. Paxton finished third and this lad should show great improvement next season. Ted Read completed a double by winning the 220, with Les Christmas beating G. R. Lowers for second place. The race of the afternoon from the spectators point of view was the 1 mile and it was a pity that Willie Nankeville was a non-starter. Len Herbert, the holder, ran a splendid race to retain his title in 4 min. 24.4 secs., and Bill Lucas just beat Derrick Burfitt for second place. Len Marchant, Vic Blowfield, Albert Frost, Jack Brown and Eric Herbert all gained standard awards, and with the men we have available I think we could take on any club in the country, at say 6 or 8 × 1 mile. New records were established in the junior sprints by Alan Sexton, his time for the 220 beating that recorded in the senior event. Harry Churcher was another record-breaker in the 2 miles Walk, and Len Herbert's time was also a new club record, and makes the times recorded about twenty years back seem very slow in comparison. items.s: MATCH AT IMBER COURT Report of a six-club track match at the Police ground, Imber Court, won by Belgrave in 1947. MATCH AT IMBER COURT Held on the fine Police ground, this match took the form of a six-sided conest and in coming out on top our lads can be said to have done well. Ted Read scored a double in the two short sprints and Jim Beaumont managed a fourth place in the 440. J. T. Cope was beaten in the 880 by Kierans in 1 min. 59.8 secs., and Jack Brown won the 1 mile in 4 min. 37 secs. Ted Stimpson showed a glimpse of his old form in winning the 2 miles in 9 min. 52 secs., and we also won the medley relay event. E. N. McKenzie was second for us in the High Jump, thus showing his versatility, Charlie Melchior won the Javelin, and Bill Sutton had a couple of second places in the Weight and Discus. Final match scores were—Belgrave H. 67. Met. Police 56. Polytechnic H. 42. Blackheath H. 41. Finchley H. 41. Dartford H. 33. Held at the News of the World ground on August 11th, and our numbers were once again on the small side, although we were pleased to see W. W. Lockyer turning out. He won the 880 yards for us and we hope that next season his work will permit him to assist us more often than this season. Alan Sexton won the 100 yards and Jim Beaumont was second in the 220. E. N. McKenzie won the 1 mile in 4 min. 38 secs., and “ Mac ” has proved a real club man in every respect and we shall miss him very much when, eventually, he goes back to his homeland. We also won the relay, but had no competitors in both jumping events, and the final match scores were—Mitcham A.C. 64. Belgrave H. 34. Epsom and Ewell H. 14. W. W. Lockyer W. W. items.s: RETURN v. SOUTH LONDON H. Report of Belgrave's return track match against South London Harriers at Tooting on 20 August 1947, lost 63 points to 33. RETURN v. SOUTH LONDON H. As the first match was so closely contested, the S.L.H. asked us to meet them again, which we did at Tooting on August 20th. They had out a very useful side and although Willie Nankeville came along to win the 880 yards, once again our sprinters were missing. With Ted Read still in the R.A.F. we naturally cannot expect him to turn out on every occasion, but without him we do not seem to win many sprint events. E. N. McKenzie was beaten by Derek Pugh in the 440, and it is interesting to recall that Pugh turned out for our junior team when still at Rutlish School. We fielded a team in the medley relay, but only because S.L.H. lent us a man, and this seems a sorry state of affairs in our club, with our membership. Result of the match was—South London H. 63 points. Belgrave H. 33 points. Willie Nankeville Willie Nankeville won the 880 yards, return match v. items.s: FINAL CLUB MEETING Report and results of Belgrave's final club meeting of handicap events at Tooting on 13 September 1947, opened by a pre-Olympic trial walk. FINAL CLUB MEETING This was held at Tooting on September 13th, and the programme consisted of club handicap events, with a pre-Olympic trial walk to open the proceedings. This was won by Jim Morris, a very fine walker, but it seemed as if Harry Churcher was a little tired, which is not to be wondered at in view of his very strenuous season on the track. The 100 yards Boys handicap was not so well supported as the previous one, and the final was won by K. Wilson (6), with S. J. Nicholas (2) second and M. Baker (3) third. The 100 yards club saw Alan Sexton (4) win a close race, beating G. B. Wood (4) with J. A. Mackenzie (7) reaping the reward of his perseverance throughout the season, gaining third place. A small field turned out for the 880 yards, and we were pleased to see D. W. Cattrall, a war-time member, make a reappearance on his return from service overseas. Alan Bishop, off 45, went away with 300 yards to go and won in 1 min. 55.5 secs., which is very good running. V. D. Wynyard (65) was second with Jim Beaumont (70) third, and the latter has also proved a good clubman throughout the season. The 2 miles run handicap saw M. Groves, off 370, make every post a winning one, and he won by 200 yards in 9 min. 22 secs., and so can have that one on the Handicapper! The rest of the field had a good tussle for second place with Vic Blowfield proving the stronger over young Arthur Bruce. Alan Sexton scored a double by winning the 300 yards, off 14, with a new member in R. B. Thomas second, and C. A. James, one of our celebrated “ twins ” who only their mother can tell apart, in third place. Full list of results hereunder:— 100 Yards Boys.—1 K. Wilson (6); 2 S. Nicholas (2); 3 M. Baker (3).
