items.s: WALKING NOTES AND RESULTS Walking column catching up on results since the last issue: Harry Churcher's 10,000 metres trials and French record in Paris (with Freddie Blackmore's report), his Dublin and Inter Counties wins, the London to Brighton, Club handicaps, the open walks, the Horwood Cup, the Club 10 Miles Championship and Police match, and hopes for the R.W.A. Junior. Although our last issue appeared in November, owing to difficulties with printing its production was held up for some time and consequently a number of results for the latter end of the track season were not shown. As these included a number of Club successes which may by now have been lost to memory or passed unnoticed by some of our less active members, the results in this issue will carry on from where I left off, viz. the 50 kilometres Championship at Eastleigh. Continuing with the 10,000 metres trials which were held during the summer, on 21st July, Harry Churcher led the field at Motspur Park, to put up the very fine time of 46.22.4, with Jack Rutland second in 49.48. A few weeks later Harry further improved on this time when, again at Motspur Park, he returned the fast time of 46.10.6, half a minute in front of Jim Morris, S.A.C. In our own promotion at the Olympic distance, Harry was not on his best form and after a tussle with Jim Morris eventually finished second. The crowning light, however, of Harry's track performances was on his visit to Paris when he set up a new French record, his time of 45.31 being 23 seconds faster than the previous best. We reproduce here the report on the race by Freddie Blackmore, Chairman of the I.A.A.F. Commission on Walking:— Paris, 7th September. Johansson's time (45.36 returned a week before at Stockholm) was much in mind as Harry Churcher and Jim Morris prepared to take on the Frenchmen Maggi and Courron at 10,000—and thus it was a great thrill to watch Harry win very comfortably in 45.31. Always within himself, he could have reduced this by 10—15 seconds and it would have been faster but for a misunderstanding at the half hour stage. It had been arranged to fire a pistol and mark the distance covered by the leader at this point, but unfortunately, the steward ran beside Harry for about 50 yards and when he actually fired the pistol Harry concluded that he was being cautioned and no doubt hoped he wouldn't feel any worse. He broke stride, eased up and took a lap to settle down again. Up to this point he had gone round with a maximum variation of 2 seconds in his lap times. After he had recovered from the shock he resumed this consistency, 1.49; 1.49; 1.50; 1.49, and so on. Meanwhile a battle royal was proceeding between Maggi and Morris with the big excited crowd on its feet. It was Churcher—Hindmar over again, only more so. Jim kept the Frenchman from getting inside, but when he concluded the Frenchman had had enough Maggi proved him wrong, got in front and stayed there to set up a new French record in two minutes faster than his previous best. Finishing times were:— H. Churcher 45.31; Maggi 45.49; Morris 46.12; Courron 46.29. Previous record 45.54.8 by Huard. In a second visit to Dublin on 20th September, Harry had a double success, winning both the mile and 2 miles. Added to all these sterling performances he won the Club Championship in a new Championship time of 14.11.2 and the Inter Counties 7 miles Championship at White City on August Monday. In the veteran class Bert East appears to have been quite prominent. On 31st July, he finished third in a Veterans A.C. Handicap, and a month later in a similar race gained first place. The Track Season terminated with our usual Club Handicap Meeting which immediately followed the 10,000 metres reported above. Bert East, still showing improvement, made his way to the front, with Harry Rouse and Reg Elson filling the other places. In the London to Brighton race which marks the end of the summer season, we encoutered the same bad luck which had befallen us in the other distance races. Ten of our walkers went off at the strike of seven, and we certainly hoped for a place at least. Colin Sutton, however, failed to please the judges at 22 miles and was ruled out. Although our other men walked up to expectations we could get no better than fourth place. Jack Baker, our first man home, was the only one to get inside nine hours. Gordon Doubleday, who completed the course in 47 minutes less time than last year, won a handicap prize presented by Charlie Poulter. The race was well supported by Club members and friends and with the weather in our favour, a good time was had by all. And so we come to the beginning of yet another winter season. This opened on 4th October, with the usual Club Handicap. 28 of our walkers turned out and a match with the Police provided an added interest. Harry Churcher soon showed that he intended to produce the same speed on the road as he had been doing on the track and eventually won by over 1½ minutes from Young Mac. with Bert East third. With our walkers in the first seven positions we had an easy win over the Police. The Novices walk on 18th October only attracted three entries and Jimmy Coates who is now developing into a nice walker won his first Club prize. The opens started as usual with the Highgate promotion over the hilly course from Parliament Hill Fields. We were without the help of Harry Churcher who was taking a well-earned rest, but with our scoring four in the first 14 we took team honours with 38 points to Enfield's 49. George Bentley was second in the handicap and the B Team second in the Team Handicap. A fortnight later in the Enfield Open, the local lads took advantage of their knowledge of the course and narrowly won from us by 3 points. And so we come once more to our own club open. Then entry of 248 individuals and 31 teams is believed to be an all-time record for a road race. Of these, 206 walkers faced the starter. Harry Churcher, racing for the first time on the road since the Club opening walk, unfortunately met with disqualification. Our old friends Surrey W.C. were out in full strength, and although we managed to secure scratch team honours it was only by the very narrow margin of one point. In the handicap section our “ C ” team secured first place and Bert East tied for third in the individual handicap. Len Fletcher's return to the field of racing was very pleasing, his position being identical with that in last year's race. Bert Webb took the prize for the first Belgrave in the scratch race without other award. The race once again received the support of many club friends whose donations to the prize fund enabled us to maintain our high standard of prizes. To them, to the R.W.A. officials, to the many club members who assisted as stewards and records, and to the clubs and individuals who supported the event we offer our most sincere thanks for their part in making the race a success. Our next event, the Horwood Cup Race on 13th December attracted 17 juniors. All our possibles for the National Junior were competing. Bert East, walking faster than ever, headed the field, and in returning a time of 56.20 set up a new championship time. Bert Webb was an easy second and George Bentley, still improving, third. Alan Robins, walking above his usual standard, won the handicap. The Boxing Day meeting produced a dozen walkers and a fine display was given by Harry Churcher and Bob McMullen. Gordon Doubleday walked well to take first place in the handicap, followed by Oliver second and Jimmy Coates third, taking his first handicap prize. So we come to the end of 1947 and embark on yet another calendar year. This opened with the Cambridge Harriers promotion at Bexley, when we returned to our last year's road form and with our scoring four in the first six secured an easy win. Harry Churcher, walking in fine style, left the rest of the field to win by nearly two minutes. Joe Coleman's last-minute effort took him up to fourth position with Len Fletcher and Bob McMullen close on his heels. The superiority of our scratch team men was further emphasised by the fact that they were placed second in the handicap section.. In the M.P.A.A. Open at Imber Court a fortnight later our walkers once again cleared the board. An added interest to the race was provided by the fact that the starters included both Harry Churcher and Jim Morris. After the first stages, however, Harry went away from Morris and at the end of the first lap was nearly a minute in front. This lead he increased over the second lap to win comfortably by a minute and a half. This time we had our scoring four in the first seven, in fact we finished 11 men in the first 21, a remarkable achievement in a field of 160. Alan Robins walked well above his usual form to win the handicap, and although he had not been included in the handicap possibles, our “ B ” team won the team event with George Bentley third in the handicap. The Club 10 Miles Championship a week later was well supported. Twenty-eight of our members turned out and with the addition of 15 policemen constituted a very fine field, a match having been arranged in conjunction with the championship. The outstanding feature of the race was Bert East's walking. After holding on to Bob McMullen for a considerable distance, he eventually left him and although finishing 2½ minutes behind Harry Churcher, who incidentally lost a little ground by taking the wrong road on the last lap, finished a minute in front of Jack Rutland to gain second place. Although we finished the first five, it looked obvious from the Police packing in mid-field that the match would be closely contested. Eventually, scoring 16 a side, we won by the narrow margin of 251 points to 277. By the time this issue is published, the R.W.A. Junior Championship at Bradford will no doubt be over. On recent form we hope to do well and in fact, add one more success to our already good record. Finally, our good wishes go to our “ Olympic ” possibles who we hope will annexe at least one title. items.s: RUNNING RESULTS. Running results section, opening with the club Three Miles Road Handicap of 4 October (50 finishers) won by L. M. Marchant, with W. E. Lucas fastest. THREE MILES ROAD HANDICAP Held on October 4th, and a record field was seen out. Len Marchant proved himself very fit by winning in fine style, and a newcomer in L. Bush was second with Ted Stimpson third. We hope that Ted will soon get back to his pre-war form which gained him an International vest It was pleasing to see old-timers such as Arthur Penny, Cecil Mains, Bert Footer, and many others still turning out for this annual event, and if numbers are any sign of strength it would seem as if we are in for a good season over the country. items.s: FIVE MILES C.C. HANDICAP Report and full result (53 runners) of the club Five Miles cross-country handicap of 25 October: V. S. Blowfield fastest, J. McDonald handicap winner; the table prints E. H. Herbert's actual time as 20.32. Held on October 25th, and again a very large field turned out including our G.O.M. of the country, George Still. George is now turned 70 years of age yet each Saturday he can be seen running over the Common, and he usually takes along a school of junior runners with him. Coming to the scratch race, this was won by Vic Blowfield with Dick Towndrow second and Ted Stimpson third. To beat the half-hour over our course is quite good running, so it can be seen that Vic put in some really fast running, which should gain him many honours before the season is over. Ron Minahan, Eric Herbert, George Chantler, and Mike Heard also ran well, and an interesting entrant was Colin Sutton, the well-known walker. The handicap was won by J. McDonald with K. R. items.s: MATCH v. OXFORD UNIVERSITY Report and placings of Belgrave's cross-country match against Oxford University at Wimbledon on 1 November, won by Belgrave 28 points to 50. Held at Wimbledon on November 1st, and we were very pleased to welcome the University runners on their first visit to our headquarters. They had sent a mixed team of first and second string runners, but proved no match for our lads, who filled the first four places. The placings in our club five miles were repeated with Vic Blowfield once again leading the field home. Scoring six aside the team result was: Belgrave H. 28 points, Oxford University 50 points. Actual placings were: 1, Blowfield 29.14; 2, Towndrow 29.20; 3, E. items.s: "BLACKSTAFFE" SHIELD C.C. RACE Report and result of the club seven miles cross-country championship for the Blackstaffe Shield on Wimbledon Common, 13 December (41 finishers), won by Vic Blowfield; sealed handicap won by S. Charlton. Our club seven miles championship was held over Wimbledon Common on December 13th, and another large field tourned out. Len Herbert, the holder, was defending his title, but in a fast run race he was beaten on the run-in by Vic Blowfield. Dick Towndrow gained his first club championship award in being third, with a past-holder in Arthur Penny fourth, and Tom Clinton fifth. The next two positions were filled by two junior members in Martin Williamson and Mike Heard. The former is up at Cambridge University while Mike has just been demobbed from the Royal Navy. These two youngsters should be a great help to our teams for many seasons to come, and to beat such experienced runners as Tom Carter, Albert Frost and Bert Mitchell was a really grand performance. The sealed handicap resulted in a win for S. Charlton, who showed much improved form, with B. Eglinton second and W. Spencer third. Eglinton is a Derby and County member who is in the R.A.F. stationed down this way, while Spencer is one of our numerous Police members. Position Name Act. Time Start Hcp. Time Postn. in Hcp. 1 V. S. items.s: "SAVAGE" SHIELD JUNIOR RACE Report and result of the club junior cross-country race for the Savage Shield, won by Martin Williamson from Eddie Short; J. W. Cook is printed 6th with a faster time (32.25) than 5th. The holder of the title, Derrick Burfitt, was a non-runner as Derrick is not doing anything over the country this season in view of the coming Olympic Games, in which he is on the list of "possibles." A very close and interesting race was seen between Eddie Short, Martin Williamson and Arthur Bruce. Eddie led for most of the way but was beaten on the run-in by Williamson, who thus won a club title in his first season with the club. We wish him long and continued success in our colours and our junior strength gives us great hopes for the future success of the club over the country. Mike Heard was unlucky in being a sufferer from that bugbear of all cross-country runners known as "stitch," and also went off the course near the end of the race and so did not finish. items.s: "MACHER" SHIELD C.C. RACE Report and result of the club 10 miles cross-country championship for the Macher Shield on 24 January, won again by Vic Blowfield; sealed handicap won by Harry Shields. Held on January 24th, this race for the club 10 miles cross-country was started, in the absence of our President, by Albert Macher. A good field of 32 runners faced the starter, including the holder Vic Blowfield, while Len Herbert and Tom Carter, 1946 winner, and Arthur Penny, winner in 1934, 1936, 1938 and 1939, also turned out. The weather was far from ideal, which is not unusual for this race, and at the half-distance Tom Clinton was leading Vic Blowfield and Frank Abberton with Len Herbert and Bill Lucas running together. When they came in sight of the finish Vic Blowfield was out in front followed by Frank Abberton, who had run a fine race, and Len Herbert beat Tom Clinton on the run-in for third position. Although Lea Herbert is recognised as our best distance runner, he has yet to win this championship, and we hope he will carry on to lead our runners in the District and National races, although at the time of writing this appears doubtful. The sealed handicap was won by that "old war-horse" Harry Shields, who battled through to the end, with Eric Herbert, maintaining his recent improved form, taking second award, and Con Abberton beating his brother Frank for third prize. items.s: CLUB BOXING DAY MEETING Report of the club's Boxing Day track meeting at Tooting Bec: 100 yards handicap won by Alan Sexton, two miles by J. W. Kennedy and three miles walk by Gordon Doubleday. Our annual track meeting was held at Tooting Bec, and although it was a really glorious morning our members were evidently still recovering from the effects of the night before, judging by the limited number who turned up. We managed to make up three heats for the 100 yards handicap, which resulted as follows: Heat 1—1, G. R. Lowers (2 yards); 2, A. C. Allen (8 yards). Heat 2—1, A. D. Sexton (3 yards); 2, W. D. Brown (2½ yards). Heat 3—1, L. G. Christmas (5½ yards); 2, F. Simmons (11 yards). The final was a grand race between the three heat winners, and in a "blanket" finish Alan Sexton was adjudged the winner with Les Christmas second and George Lowers third. The field for the two miles run was more numerous, although both Len Herbert and Derrick Burfitt were non-starters. The eventual winner was J. W. Kennedy off 350 yards, who put in a storming finish to beat Alan Bishop (260) with Eric Bishop (350) third. The three miles walking handicap was won by Gordon Doubleday, who turns out over the country and yet still manages to put up good performances when he switches over to walking events. G. R. Lowers G. items.sum: Preview of the 1948 track season: a coaching panel under George Clay, club championships at Tooting Bec on 5 June, planned junior and inter-club fixtures, and entries to the Running Hon. Secretary E. A. Duffett.
items.s: REVIEW OF COMING TRACK SEASON Preview of the 1948 track season: a coaching panel under George Clay, club championships at Tooting Bec on 5 June, planned junior and inter-club fixtures, and entries to the Running Hon. Secretary E. A. Duffett. The thoughts of our club members will now be turning towards training for the track season, and they will be pleased to know that your committee have gone into the question of coaching, and have appointed a panel of coaches under the supervision of George Clay. George is well known to those of our members who train at Motspur Park and club members will also recall his son Fred, who was a very good sprinter and later took up the 440 yards. Fuller details will be given to members at a later date, but I can assure you that George is going into the question of training schedules very thoroughly and will be only too pleased to help any member who wishes to improve his performance by training to a definite schedule. This being Olympic Games year, we are all hoping to see some of our members in the English team, and in view of the date of the Games, we have put our club championships earlier in the season than is usual. They will be held at Tooting Bec Track on Saturday, June 5ith, and it is hoped that members will "book" this date and support the championships to their utmost. For members' guidance a provisional list of club fixtures can be seen at the end of the Gazette, although we hope to arrange further fixtures as the season approaches. We have arranged our usual Junior match with the Whitgift Middle School at Croydon, and have also accepted invitations to take part in Junior inter-club contests with the Polytechnic H. and Highgate H. The "Gordon-Stewart" Trophy contest, of which we are the holders, is being held at Drayton Green Track on Saturday, May 8th, and we have also arranged matches with the L.A.C., Cambridge H., Shaftesbury H., Highgate H., Mitcham A.C., and the Metropolitan Police A.C. The club have booked Tooting Bec Track for several dates, and we have had to take some Monday dates, in view of the number of clubs now using Tooting for meetings, but I trust this will not deter our members from turning up in better numbers than they did last season. With the Olympic Games being the highlight of the season, I think the usual club programme will rather be oversshadowed, but with all the "cracks" concentrating on that vital period from Friday, July 30th, to Saturday, August 7th, when all the athletic events are being held, this should give some of our less prominent members a chance of proving themselves. All entries and enquiries should be sent to the Running Hon. Secretary, as under: E. A. DUFFETT, 57, Harcourt Road, Thornton Heath, Surrey. items.s: Editorial notes apologising for the gap since the February issue and reporting the 61st Annual General Meeting, its honours awards and the new officers, captains and committee. Owing to various circumstances outside our control it has not been possible to issue the Belgravian as regularly as had been anticipated. It will be noticed that this is the first issue since February and many items have had to be passed over and others dealt with briefly. It is hoped that we will be able to publish more frequently in the future. * * * The 61st Annual General Meeting held at Belgrave Hall on Saturday, October 9th, was perhaps the biggest ever, as nearly one hundred and fifty members were present. The Hon. Secretary's report, which had been printed and circulated, was taken as read and the Hon. Treasurer explained in some detail the Balance Sheet. Upon the recommendation of the Committee it was unanimously agreed to award Honours Badges to Alan Sexton and Jack Stirling Wakeley: Alan for his A.A.A. and Southern A.A.A. successes in the Junior 220 yards championships and Jack for his wonderful performance in the 24 hours' walk which he won by covering 122 miles 1,411 yards. These two are special awards needing the endorsement of the Meeting, and this was readily given. We must also congratulate Alf Taylor on having the honour of Life Member bestowed upon him. Alf has done a large amount of thankless "Back Room" work, principally on the Social side, and few will forget the manner of his handling of our junior cross country members three seasons back; so that the honour is well deserved. Upon the recommendation of the Committee and with the unanimous approval of the Meeting, Bill Webb was elected to the Presidential Chair for the ensuing twelve months. In thanking the meeting for the honour they were bestowing upon him, he said that increasing family ties, plus anno domini, had finally caused him to relinquish the office of Hon. Treasurer, which he had held since 1924. Syd King (and his wife) were elected to the vacant office. Several new appointments were made: E. T. Bateman taking over the Field Events; Frank Simmons the Junior Section; Micky Pyer, Junior Coach; and new blood was introduced amongst the captains by the election of Vern Blowfield, Ted Stimpson, Len Grimshaw and Len Fletcher. The elected Committee have been strengthened by newcomers in Bert Mitchell, Dick Towndrow, Len Grimshaw and Bill True. So that with the "old'uns" hanging on we may look forward to even better times than those we have already celebrated. Alan Sexton Alan Sexton awarded Honours Badge for A.A.A. and Southern A.A.A. items.sum: Notes on the Olympic Games: Jimmie Bellchambers and Harry Evans appointed walking judges, and the Games performances of Bill Lucas, Willie Nankeville, Harry Churcher and Etienne Gailly, with greetings from Gailly and news of Fred Rowell.
items.s: Olympic Games. Notes on the Olympic Games: Jimmie Bellchambers and Harry Evans appointed walking judges, and the Games performances of Bill Lucas, Willie Nankeville, Harry Churcher and Etienne Gailly, with greetings from Gailly and news of Fred Rowell. Our congratulations to Jimmie Bellchambers and Harry Evans upon their appointment as Walking Judges. To have such an honour bestowed upon them is a mark of appreciation of merit and ability from the "powers that be." In their time both Jimmie and Harry were distinguished competitors, both having won high honours on the track and road, and they are still enthusiastic workers, both in the Committee room and at our sports meetings. For many seasons now they have officiated at all the main Championship meetings, both summer and winter. Most of the original nominations of members for the Olympics, for one reason or another came "unstuck" at the final trials, but a new star arose in Bill Lucas to join company with Harry Churcher, Willie Nankeville and Rene Howell. Bill Lucas was selected for the 5,000 metres because of his 3rd in the A.A.A. 3 miles championship. Bill eventually finished 7th in his heat in about 15 mins. 29 secs. Willie Nankeville ran magnificently in the 1,500 metres. His second place in the heat, about 15 yards behind the winner, Erikson of Sweden, in 3 mins. 55.8 secs., was an excellent performance and showed that Willie could use his head as well as his feet. The day of the final turned out very wet and the general conditions were none too good for either competitor or spectator. The race itself was very fast and Willie running exceptionally, eventually finished 6th in 3 mins. 52.6 secs., just under three seconds behind the winner, a time which before 1932 would have won an Olympic title. What really happened to Harry Churcher in the 10,000 metres walk we shall probably never know. He, however, won his heat in 46 mins. 26.4 secs., two seconds inside Olympic record. In the final, a "caution" in the early part of the race worried Harry considerably and he perceptibly steadied himself and afterwards never seemed comfortable and appeared to have lost confidence, finishing 5th in 46 mins. 28 secs. Of Etienne Gailly, running for his country—Belgium—better known to some of us during the war as "Steve" and his very gallant effort in the Marathon will probably be talked of in the future almost as much as the memorable "Dorando" marathon. Etienne led practically all the way and was first to enter the Stadium but he had run himself to a standstill and was eventually third, his time being 2 hrs. 35 mins. 33 secs. Since returning to Belgium he competed in the Inter Allied Games held in Antwerp and finished second in the 5,000 metres and he came back again to England in September and was second in the Britannia Shield cross country race at Halton. Etienne sends greetings to the Club and wishes to thank his many Belgrave friends for their kind wishes and thoughts. We were pleased to renew acquaintance with Fred Rowell, another war-time member; this journey he was Manager of the Canadian Olympic Athletic Team. items.h: Seen at Wembley during the Olympic Games.
items.sum: Light-hearted round-up of Belgrave members seen officiating and helping at Wembley and the road events during the 1948 Olympic Games.
items.s: Seen at Wembley during the Olympic Games. Light-hearted round-up of Belgrave members seen officiating and helping at Wembley and the road events during the 1948 Olympic Games. Our Running Hon. Secretary as Marksman, ensuring that the World's fastest athletes didn't have their fingers ⅛in. in advance of the correct position at the starts. He must be an expert now on starting blocks; and was probably glad he wasn't called upon to handicap the fields on accustomed A.A.A. standard times at any rate! Bert Ellsey judging Field Events and standing up well to the strain of hours of competition. Our announcer's voice (Arthur Cook to you) floating over the air. Harry Evans and Jimmy Belchamber judging the walkers; Syd Roberts stewarding and producing mysterious jugs of refreshment for the monarchs of the Judges' stand and doing a grand job on the Road Walk. Harry Parker recording on Marathon and Road Walk and sitting tight at other times when it rained too hard, ably assisted by Jack Chapple! Our General Hon. Secretary taking things easy after discharging his responsibilities on the 50 Kilos Walk—except when seen sprinting around the track from Judges to Chief Judge during the Track Walk; Dick Savage, a busy man of Road Walk and Marathon days, in charge of a coach; Charlie Poulter, Syd King, Percy Wright and their battalions of assistants all doing great work on the Road Walk; George Chantler first and last pointsman on the Marathon, an arrangement which permitted a good view of all that happened in the Stadium. Not forgetting Joe Turner with an "Omega" in his hand and sitting astride a white bench. And last, but not least, our portly friend and adviser, Wally Jewell, assistant referee and chief judge, complete with pencil and scoring cards and visibly thinning under the strain of the "photo finishes"; and away at Herne Hill Track Dr. Woodard was acting as chief medico to the cyclists. Chief Insp. Jack Bidgood was "on the job" for both Road Walk and Marathon, supervising the courses throughout their length. Yes, Belgrave were well in evidence—on the track competing for the honour of Britain, in the crowd witnessing unforgetable sport and performances—and wherever wanted, giving a hand with the big and little jobs which go to make up the tremendous organisation of the World's largest sports meeting. The Senior, Junior and Youths championships were held at Aylesford on February 28th and it speaks well for the arrangements that these three races were carried through on the same afternoon. The hospitality extended by the local Paper Mills was on the highest scale and will long be remembered by the competitors and officials alike. In the Junior (under 21) event there were 20 teams and we did well to finish in 6th place. Eddie Short led our team home in 6th position, Mike Heard was 12th, Eric Bishop 27, and Len Bishop 68. Others to finish were: L. A. Adams 83, R. Garwood 88, and S. G. Brooks 106. Len Herbert was coming through well and Frank Abberton and Tom Clinton were also well placed. items.sum: Report of the English (National) cross country championships at Graves Park, Sheffield, where Belgrave won the senior team title for their fourth National victory, with Vic Blowfield second to Sydney Wooderson.
items.s: The English C.C. Championships. Report of the English (National) cross country championships at Graves Park, Sheffield, where Belgrave won the senior team title for their fourth National victory, with Vic Blowfield second to Sydney Wooderson. These were held in Graves Park, Sheffield, on March 13th, and being a fine day a very large crowd watched the racing. There were tremendous fields for all three races, Senior, Junior and Youths. Once again Sydney Wooderson was up the front but this time there was a small bunch of runners with him including our own Vic Blowfield. On the last lap Wooderson made his effort but Vic kept with him stride for stride and then about half-a-mile from the finish Vic made a gallant attempt to get away from his man and succeeded up to a point. The only snag was that there was further to go than Vic had thought and Wooderson came again to beat Vic up the finishing straight. Len Herbert had run well throughout as had Ted Stimpson, now getting back to his pre-war form, and with Frank Abberton also making a last lap effort, and Tom Carter and Tommy Clinton coming along well we found to our satisfaction that we had beaten Sutton Harriers, the holders, to record our fourth National victory. Les Stokell was once again a good 7th man and Albert Frost and Dick Tobin completed our team. Positions were: 2 V. S. Blowfield; 12 L. W. Herbert; 15 E. S. Stimpson; 27 F. J. Abberton; 41 C. T. Carter; 57 T. P. Clinton; 64 C. L. Stokell; 95 A. E. Frost; 132 R.W. Tobin. Team scores were: 1 Belgrave H., 154; 2 Sutton H., 174; 3 Blackheath H., 183. In the Junior race Eddie Short was again our first man home in 7th position, and to gain such a high place in a race speaks well for Eddie's strength and determination. Mike Heard also ran well in finishing 40th and Arthur Bruce ran pluckily on a damaged foot to be 56th, with Eric Bishop 65, R. Garwood 112, L. C. Bishop 117, and L. A. Adams 138. In the team race we were placed 8th out of an entry of 30 clubs so can be well satisfied. items.label: No. 104
items.sum: Report of the London to Brighton road relay promoted by the News of the World, won by Belgrave in 3 hrs. 57 mins. 29 secs. after Bill Lucas overtook Max Jones on the last lap, with a stage-by-stage account.
items.s: The Brighton Relay. Report of the London to Brighton road relay promoted by the News of the World, won by Belgrave in 3 hrs. 57 mins. 29 secs. after Bill Lucas overtook Max Jones on the last lap, with a stage-by-stage account. The classic of the road relays, "the Brighton," promoted by the News of the World, was held on April 10th, starting from Mitcham Common. The weather was kind, there being bright sunshine without much heat, and a large party of supporters accompanied the team along the road. The finish of the race was most dramatic and those of us who saw Bill Lucas start off thirty-one seconds behind the Birchfielder on the last lap, thought it was all over bar shouting, and continued in a rather leisurely way into Brighton. Bill, however, had other views and maintained that lazy-looking but devastating stride of his right up to Max Jones who was leading. Max was unable to respond to Bill's challenge and there was a mighty roar from the crowd when it was realised what was happening and Bill eventually reached the finishing line just 20 seconds to the good. Truly a wonderful finish and reminiscent of that of years ago when Brickwood of Mitcham beat our own Arthur Allum in the finishing straight. The start of the race was far from impressive from our point of view, Ted Stimpson being unable to keep the fast pace set by the other runners and finished at Purley Corner 71 seconds in arrears. Tom Clinton ran a good leg and handed over to George Lucas at Merstham in sixth place. George started with supreme confidence on his 4½ miles jaunt up Redhill and along the switchback to the Prince Albert where he handed over in second place, clocking 22 mins. 36 secs., only 4 secs. slower running than Birchfield who were now leading. Over the next stretch of nearly five miles, Tom Carter took us to within two seconds of the leader. Ken Stimpson on the next stage to the Half Moon at Crawley, about 3½ miles—easily passed his opponent and handed over to Martin Williamson well in the lead. Martin ran extremely well to maintain this advantage to Handcross with a margin of 13 seconds in hand. The next leg to Hickstead, about six miles, is considered as perhaps the stiffest and most important, and Vernon Blowfield was up against Bobby Reid, "Sidney" and Stan Belton (Surrey). After a terrific struggle Vern. was barely a yard ahead of Reid at the change over, with Wooderson some distance in the rear. On to the foot of Dale Hill, about 4¾ miles, Len Herbert was never comfortable and eventually finished 35 secs. behind the Stagbearers. Eddie Short had Dale Hill to climb (shades of Bert Footer) but ran splendidly, in to Pycombe, although he was only able to reduce the Stagbearers lead by 4 secs., and so on to the Brighton front to see Bill Lucas turn the corner of the Aquarium ahead, to our frenzied delight. The time for the whole journey, 3 hrs. 57 mins. 29 secs., was the fourth fastest in the present series. items.sum: Report of the newly instituted Surrey County road relay at Woking, won by Belgrave, who became the first holders of the Underhill Trophy.
items.s: Surrey County Road Relay. Report of the newly instituted Surrey County road relay at Woking, won by Belgrave, who became the first holders of the Underhill Trophy. This newly instituted championship was held at Woking on the 25th September and nine clubs entered teams of six men, each to run a lap of just under three miles. Willie Nankeville, our A.A.A. 1 mile champion, led off and gave us the lead from Surrey and Mitcham. Len Marchant kept the lead and then Stan Davies went off and running with a badly blistered foot he allowed the Surrey men to get within two seconds of him. Eddie Short went next and running a well judged race went right away to give us a 40 seconds lead. Archie Bedford was our next and he kept the lead so that Bill Lucas ran home an easy winner in 1 hr. 30 mins. 27 secs. Surrey A.C. were next in 1 hr. 32 mins. 5 secs. and Mitcham A.C. third in 1 hr. 34 mins. 24secs. We thus became the first holders of the "Underhill" Trophy awarded to the winning team, and our thanks go to the Old Woking Club for the splendid tea which they provided after the race. items.s: With our Road Men. Notes on Belgrave members in open road races during 1948, including wins by Tom Clinton and Dick Towndrow, the club Marathon championship won by Frank Abberton for the new A. F. Mitchell trophy, and A.A.A. standard medals. Quite a number of members have been competing in open road races this season and "Champ" Smith has done a good job in keeping them together. We were also pleased to see Bert Footer out again and showing that he is still a force to be reckoned with at distance running. Tom Clinton has also done very well and he won the Portsmouth A.C. 10 miles race on March 29th when we finished second in the team race with Tom Carter 7th and Dick Tobin 11th completing our team. George Chantler finished 6th but was running for our "B" team who were placed 4th while our "C" team finished 6th out of an entry of nine teams. On the 17th April in the Walton 10 miles race, Tom Clinton finished first with Tom Carter fifth, Geoff Pearson 14th and Bert Mitchell 16th. We won the team race beating Reading. Dick Towndrow won the 15 miles road race promoted by the Wigmore Harriers, and Geoff Pearson and Con Abberton finished equal fifth. In the Finchley "20" Geoff Pearson was 17th in 2 hrs. 13 mins. 31 secs., quite a creditable effort. On the 8th May our lads went to Chichester for the 16 miles road race to Portsmouth and Dick Tobin was our first runner in 8th place, Bert Footer 9th, Bert Smith 10, George Chantler 14, Con Abberton 15, J. McDonald 18, Tom Carter 24, and as we had entered two teams they actually tied for third place in the team race and Bert Footer won the toss for "B" team as to whom should take the prizes. items.s: The Track Season. Review of the 1948 track season: Belgrave members at the Olympic Games, Alan Sexton's A.A.A. Junior 220 yards title, junior relay successes, the Youths section, and the retained Gordon Stewart Trophy. On the whole I think we can be said to have had a fairly successful season and we had the satisfaction of seeing three of our club members compete in the Olympic Games as members of the Great Britain team. Actually another member, E. Gailly, was a member of the Belgium team and put up a magnificent performance in finishing third in the Marathon race. Will Nankeville also ran the "race of his life" by finishing 6th in the 1,500 metres final and when one looked through the list of those qualifying for the final, this was indeed a sterling performance. Harry Churcher and Bill Lucas also performed well without actually "hitting the high-spots" and cannot be said to have let the team down, rather was it a question of our men being outclassed by the wealth of opposition they were up against. We also competed in the "Kinnaird" Trophy and "Waddilove" events and also took part in an inter-club contest at the opening of the new sports stadium at Brighton. An encouraging feature was the promise shown by some of our Junior members and in Alan Sexton we have one of the finest young sprinters in the country. Alan crowned a successful season by winning the A.A.A. Junior 220 yards championship and another good performance at this meeting was Michael Paxton's win in the 440 yards. Our Junior sprint relay teams also did well in winning the Surrey County 4 x 110 yards and being placed second in the A.A.A Junior event against strong opposition. We are badly in need of a few first class sprinters for our senior matches as Lionel Grimshaw had muscle trouble and Gordon Lowers was not always available. Len Marchant and John Cope were our mainstays in the middle distance events and as usual we always had plenty of men to call on for the long distance races. Micky Pyer has been looking after our Youths section and has made a first-class "discovery" in M. J. Stearman. This lad looks a second Derrick Burfitt, having much the same style, and he won the Surrey County Youths 1 mile title in fine style. Also at this meeting D. E. Marshall won the 220 yards and being a school-mate of Alan Sexton's we expect still better performances in the future. Charlie Smart came home from Germany to compete in the A.A.A. meeting and ran well in both the six and the three miles without quite catching the selector's eye. George Lucas and Len Herbert had what was to them rather a disappointing season and we hope that a full season over the country will see them both fighting fit for next track season. Reg. Ruddick won the Surrey County 6 miles track title and should prove a great help to our teams when he is qualified to represent us. We once again won the "Gordon Stewart" Trophy put up by Ealing Harriers and had many enjoyable matches against both new and old friends. E. Gailly E. items.sum: The cross-country correspondent's look back at last season's successes and preview of the coming season's fixtures, from the Surrey Youths race to the English championships and Brighton Relay.
e: South of the Thames Cross Country Championships
items.s: OVER THE COUNTRY. The cross-country correspondent's look back at last season's successes and preview of the coming season's fixtures, from the Surrey Youths race to the English championships and Brighton Relay. I said at the opening of last cross country season, that given a fair “rub of the green” we had the men who could sweep the board, so far as the “open” championships were concerned, and I must say that our lads more than justified our high hopes. To win practically all the major events of the cross country season and then carry on to win the “classic” London to Brighton Relay was, I think, a performance that will take a great deal of beating. With the help of Dick Towndrow, and such as Archie Bedford, Eddie Short, Mike Heard, “Ginger” Kennedy and Jack Brown, to mention only a few of our promising members plus the help of last season's stalwarts, I think we shall have yet another successful year over the country. December 4th sees the first of the County championships with the Surrey Youths race, and youngsters between the ages of 16 and 18 who wish to compete should turn up at Belgrave Hall and contact Micky Pyer who is in charge of the training of our juniors over the country. The following Saturday we have the first of our Club Championships and as there is a sealed handicap in conjunction here is an opportunity for all members, both fast and slow, to show their paces. On December 18th we have our 5 miles (under 21) race for the Savage Shield, and here again we are holding a handicap open to all members between the ages of 16 and 21. Boxing Day sees the usual track meeting at Tooting Common and there are events open to sprinters, runners, walkers and shot putters, so make a note of sending in your name and don't forget the meeting starts at 11 a.m., as last year a few turned up in the afternoon and so had a wasted journey. New Year's Day is County Championship day and we shall have teams in both the Surrey and Middlesex County events, as our members who are qualified to run in the latter race compete as members of the Cadogan A.C. and should contact Frank Webb if they wish to enter. On January 15th we have a visit from the Thames Valley Harriers for a social run. January 29th is the day of our club 10 miles race for the “Macher Shield” and we shall be pleased to see our old friend Albert Macher present the shield to the winner. We then come to the “open” championships and on February 12th the South of the Thames 7 miles race is due to be held at Horsham, followed a fortnight later by the Southern Counties events at Sandhurst. March 12th is the day of the English cross-country championships and the venue is the Bromford Bridge Racecourse at Birmingham. We can be sure that Birchfield Harriers will make a strong bid for the title on their own door-step, but hope that once again we can bring the title down South, and given the proper support I am sure we can do it. We then have the usual crop of open Road relays, culminating in the London to Brighton race, which if we win this year, will set up a new record for the total number of wins by any one club but will also be our second hat-trick of victories, a feat also performed by no other club. As usual we shall have our supporters coaches on the road and those wishing to book seats should make early application to the Social Hon. Secretary, Dave Shepherd. It will be noticed that we have “B” team matches and these are intended for those members who do not get a chance to represent the club in the big races. We hope to arrange more of these as the season progresses and members wishing to take part should keep in touch with the cross-country captain, Alf Taylor. Once again I wish all our members a very successful season and any further information as regards fixtures, training, etc., I shall be only too pleased to help in any way I can. E. A. items.sum: Review of the walkers' 1948 season, including Harry Churcher's National 10 miles win, world 5 miles record and Olympic 10,000 metres, the Nijmegen Shield win and Jack Stirling Wakeley's 24 hours walk.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Review of the walkers' 1948 season, including Harry Churcher's National 10 miles win, world 5 miles record and Olympic 10,000 metres, the Nijmegen Shield win and Jack Stirling Wakeley's 24 hours walk. In our last issue comment was made on our chances of a win in the Junior Championship this year and everyone was very hopeful of adding another one to our many successes in this race. However we have yet another year to wait. The race this year was held at Bradford and at about 7½ miles, after it looked as though we were in a fairly comfortable position, Bert East failed to please the judges and was ruled out. Bert Webb and George Bentley, who had walked together almost throughout, maintained their positions at 4th and 5th and after Bill True and Don Heath had been told of the loss of East, they both got down to it and succeeded in carrying our team into 2nd position. Next year we hope to have the services of Joe Scamell in addition to some new members when our chances should be even better than this year. The Surrey County 10 miles Championship provided us with an easy win, our team being led home by Harry Churcher. In addition to gaining the first two places in the Individual Championship and taking Team honours, our “B” Team were placed 3rd. Our Middlesex Walkers did not meet with quite so much success. After Jack Rutland had received one of his few disqualifications, our Cadogan team managed to finish 3rd, Enfield beating us into the place by 1 point. A fortnight later thousands of Londoners witnessed the first athletic event ever to be held in Hyde Park and saw Harry Churcher cut out a terrific pace which took him further in front at every step. The race was, of course, the National 10 miles Championship and Harry's time of 75.10.4 must be the fastest ever accomplished on the road. Needless to say, he retained his title as also did the Club in the Team event. We, therefore, become the initial holders of two new trophies—The London Shield given by the Evening News, and the Ingram St. Dunstans Cup given by Mr. Ingram of St. Dunstans. Bert Ea[illegible]t of the “B” Team walked well to finish 8th and get a place in the Surrey Team which tied with Middlesex for 1st place and contained three of our men, viz., Harry Churcher, Charlie Churcher and Bert East. Of 23 teams to finish, our “B” Team was placed 6th, only 10 points behind the third team. The following week Charlie Churcher took a small team down to Chichester for the trek from there to Portsmouth. The race resulted in Charlie setting up a new course record. Bert Clayton walked well to finish 4th and with Alan Robins and Joe Wilson making the second half of the team, we finished 2nd to Enfield. In the postponed Woodford Green Open the following week we were without Harry and Charlie Churcher, and although our lads were well placed, with Bob Readman (3rd) leading them home, we could only get second to the promoting club who naturally were out in full strength. The Regents Park 15 proved the biggest catastrophe of the season. Apart from Charlie Churcher, who although beaten into 2nd position by Charlie Megnin and returned almost same time as last year, everything went wrong. Our “A” Team men were disqualified almost in a procession. First Bert East, then Colin Sutton and then Joe Coleman. Despite this we managed to finish 4th one place in front of the “B” Team who gave a good account of themselves. The following week we were invited to take a team down to Halton for a match with the R.A.F. Although the majority of our opponents were Air Force Apprentices they showed great keenness and it looks at if Fred Herring is going to produce some real talent in a couple of years' time. After the race we were entertained to a first class meal and a good time was had by all. And so to the National 20 at Sudbury. Our teams were supported by what must be the biggest crowd of Club Members and friends ever seen at a road race. Our Road Captain, Charlie Churcher, surprised most people by not adopting his usual get-a-way method and the opening stages of the race were unusually slow. Later on, however, Charlie developed stomach trouble and was obliged to fall back. About the same time Colin Sutton had trouble with his shoes and lost a lot of ground. In the centre of the field, however, our Vice Captain, Jack Bidgood, was doing some excellent work holding together about half a dozen of our walkers which no doubt had much to do with the ultimate result of the race. On recovering from his trouble, Colin Sutton battled bravely on recovering position after position and eventually caught up on Jack Bidgood and Co. Charlie, however, had continued to drop back and with our friends, Surrey W.C., holding two places in the first five, a win for us seemed out of the question. Eventually our lads finished in a procession with five consecutive placings from 18 to 22 and backed up by George Bentley, Joe Wilson and Joe Coleman, we succeeded in taking the Nijmegen Shield with our eight walkers in the first 48, an excellent performance on which all are to be congratulated. In the meantime the Track Season had opened with a 2 mile walk handicap on 1st May. Naturally the entry was not very big and the race was won by our Track Captain, in the fast time of 14.19 with Syd King 2nd and Joe Scamell 3rd. Three weeks later the second Track Handicap attracted a much larger entry and resulted in a win for Don Heath with Bill True 2nd and young Jimmie Coates 3rd. On the same evening a not too successful Novices' race was held, the only two competitors being introduced by the aforementioned Jimmie Coates. The following Saturday we sent a team to Leicester for the “Round the City” Walk and against strong opposition came out winners, a good omen for the 50 kilometres. And so we come to the most notable success in the Club's history for many years—our Track Captain's achievement in setting up a new World's record for 5 miles. Unfortunately this was held on the same day as the Club Championships and Harry was therefore deprived of the Club support which he deserved. Our thanks are due to Surrey W.C. who so ably assisted in the management of the race in the absence of our own members who were unable to be present. Following this splendid effort, Harry then went to Tooting and successfully defended his two miles title, holding off Bob McMullen and Joe Coleman who finished 2nd and 3rd respectively. The following Monday we staged our increasingly popular Inter Club Contest at Tooting. An entry of nine teams was one more than last year and all the four races were well supported. The total of 55 walkers was an increase of 14 over the previous year. In the absence of Harry Churcher and Bob McMullen, our chances of success were much reduced, but we eventually came out winners with 106 points to Highgate Harriers 102 with Surrey W.C. 3rd. In the Southern Counties 2 miles Championship at Uxbridge, four of our walkers competed and once again Harry led the field to win in the excellent time of 13.53, eleven seconds in front of Jim Morris and beating Bert Cooper's 1935 time of 13.54. Mac and Joe both succeeded in gaining Southern Standards. And so we come to the last R.W.A. National Championship, the 50 Kilometres, which was held at Birmingham. After our win at Leicester, we had great hopes of gaining our 2nd National Success of the season, but what seemed on paper a good team, failed to materialise. At the half distance, both Bert Clayton and Colin Sutton were forced to retire and although Pat Sapcote and Joe Wilson walked exceedingly well, they were not good enough to get the team a place. However, they both retain their “Junior” status and with Pat Sapcote rapidly improving, he should be a big asset to the teams next year. Jack Bidgood walking as well as ever, led the team home in 12th position with Charlie Churcher two places behind and both qualified for standard medals. Surprise of the race was the excellent performance of Lloyd Johnson who finished 2nd to Rex Whitlock and gave the Olympic Selectors something to think about. On the same day, our fast track men competed in the Kinnaird meeting Team Race, and with the team being led by Harry Churcher scored a convincing win over Highgate Harriers with our Surrey friends third. Our annual Mob Match with Surrey Walking Club at Tooting Bec attracted the very large entry of 35 and scoring 10 aside we emerged the winners. George Atkinson won the sealed handicap with veteran Charlie Speechley 2nd and Alan Robins 3rd. At the White City on 3rd and 10th July respectively, Harry Churcher secured a double win in the 2 and 7 miles walks and with these following on his previous successes, we had great hopes for him at Wembley in the 10,000 metres. However, perhaps a very heavy summer programme had some effect on Harry, because when the big day came, he was obviously not on his best form, and although he won his heat comfortably, in the final on the Saturday, he was fifth to J. Michaelsson of Sweden. The first five however beat the previous Olympic Record. On 13th/14th August the Surbiton Town Sports Club, with the assistance of Ernie Neville, promoted a 24 hours track walk. Our only competitor, Jack Stirling Wakeley, was known to have been doing some very hard training, and after maintaining an almost even pace throughout the 24 hours, won by the huge margin of 10 miles, having covered the distance of 122 miles 1,411 yards. A month later we came to the Annual London to Brighton Trek and our entry of 12 competitors was the biggest since 1938. Unfortunately Jack Baker was unable to get to the start, but even so we still had hopes of a place. After doing about 35 miles, however, Jack Bidgood was forced to retire with blistered feet and with the remaining men making a brave effort, we had again to be content with 4th place, Team honours going to Surrey W.C. Jack Wakeley, first man home for the club in 12th place, thus becomes this year's holder of the “Belgrave” Cup. Perhaps the most surprising performance of all was that of George Oliver, who, competing in his first Brighton, finished 18th, just outside first class standard and very deservedly won a special handicap prize presented by Charlie Poulter. Thus we come to the end of another Club Year. Successes we have had as well as misfortunes and disappointments. One thing is certain, many of our walkers are reaching the veteran stage and will soon need replacing by younger members if we are to maintain our position as one of the leading clubs. In the current season, every effort should be made to increase the number of Junior walkers as it is hoped to have a sufficient number to put on the race for the new Junior (under 21) Cup presented to the Club by Tommy Green and also to form the basis of some strong teams for the future. items.label: No. 104
items.sum: A run of short club notes: news of members at home, abroad and in the Services, appointments, a death, novices' races, social evenings and coaching.
items.s: A run of short club notes: news of members at home, abroad and in the Services, appointments, a death, novices' races, social evenings and coaching. Sunday morning strolls have recommenced and start from Wimbledon Station at 9.30 under the guidance of Charles Churcher. Both runners and walkers are welcome. * * * * Battersea Park Track has been re-opened for training but sports meetings will not be allowed for some time yet. * * * * A Get Fit Class will be conducted by our Chief Coach, George Clay, at Belgrave Hall each Tuesday evening, commencing January 4th, at 7.15. Sprinters are particularly invited to attend. * * * * Charlie Smart who although now “almost” settled in Germany is, however, still busy training and racing. He sends his greetings and hopes to be back for some of the big championships, time and circumstance permitting. * * * * George Clay passed the A.A.A. Grade 2 Coaching test, first time. Hearty congratulations, George. He has also passed the County Judges Official test. * * * * Max Quackenbos, now settled in New Jersey, sends greetings and regrets he was unable to get over for the Games. * * * * Wally Rispin, who helped us in many team races in pre-war days, is back with Blackpool & Fylde where he was the leading runner during the last winter season. * * * * We are indebted to Fred Brunning for a new urn at Belgrave Hall. * * * * Wilf Anderson, who is off to Germany on a tour of duty and may not be back for some months, sends greetings to his many friends. * * * * Dan Patience, who is now happily married, has settled in Scotland and the proud possessor of a bonny son—whom we have now welcomed as a Belgravian. * * * * Congratulations to “Ian Michael” on his selection of fathers. I understand his Mother is doing well, but what about poor old Joe? Ian has already been nominated as a member by his grandfather, Tommy Askew. Tommy, I understand, has just celebrated his Golden Wedding Anniversary. Congrats, Tommy. * * * * Sergt. Bernard Eglinton writes that the R.A.F. have moved him to Ismalia where there is a track on which he is trying to perform. He sends greetings to all. * * * * Jack Shields and Johnny Briggs went up to Oxford University for the Michaelmas Term and we wish them well academically and athletically. * * * * Geoff. Osmint, now a gunner in B.A.O.R., sends greetings and says he couldn't attend the A.G.M. for this reason. * * * * A cheery letter arrived recently from Life Member Ernie Musselbrook, a former cross country captain, with all good wishes to the Club. * * * * Our good wishes go to Len Cheesley and Julian de Ruyter who have recently been swallowed up by the Services. * * * * Incidentally it is not generally known that by a Committee ruling there is no obligation on members called to the Services under the National Service Act to pay subscriptions, if they have notified their translation from civilian life. Of course if finances are good the Hon. Treasurer would like to hear from you but it's up to you! * * * * Willie Nankeville has resigned and says he intends devoting his time to building up the local newly formed club, Old Woking A.C. * * * * Martin Williamson, our Junior Cross Country champion, is already busy on the track and recently won the Mile for St. Catherines College at the Cambridge University Freshmen's Meeting, and represented Cambridge University v. Oxford in the Inter-Varsity Relays on November 20th. * * * * Len Camin is busy as Hon. Secretary of the Eltham United F.C., but still hopes to show his paces on the track. * * * * On December 11th there are 3 miles novices races for walkers and runners, so interest your unattached friends right away and bring them along to try themselves out. * * * * At long last the Belgrave Winter “Secret” has been disclosed to members. But one date has yet to be revealed—the date of the Ricketts Shield Race—sorry cads! * * * * Les Cohen has recently been appointed Assistant Hon. Secretary of the Southern Counties C.C. Association; Jack Chapple has been appointed to a similar office in the South of Thames Association C.C. and Ernie Duffett has been elected a Vice President to the same Association. * * * * We all deeply regret the passing of George Hogsflesh, for so many years Assistant Secretary of the Amateur Athletic Association. He probably had more friends in athletics than any other man. * * * * Social evenings, preceded by a sit-down tea, will be held at Belgrave Hall on the following Saturdays: December 11th; January 29th; and February 19th. items.sum: The new President, W. G. Webb, thanks members for electing him, calls for co-operation and team spirit, and thanks them for the clock presented on his resignation as Treasurer.
items.s: From the President The new President, W. G. Webb, thanks members for electing him, calls for co-operation and team spirit, and thanks them for the clock presented on his resignation as Treasurer. FROM THE PRESIDENT I take this opportunity of expressing my appreciation and thanks for the honour you have conferred on me by electing me President of the Club. There is no honour of which I could be more proud. I am deeply aware of the responsibility of this office and will do my best to carry on in the tradition of my predecessors. In this endeavour I shall be guided by the light they have left burning and sustained by the confidence that I shall have the co-operation of all members. Nothing is more important to the Club than this spirit of co-operation. Our continued success both in administration and in the field of sport must, in the end, depend on the strength of each member's personal sense of responsibility for the affairs of the Club. We must never allow ourselves to leave everything to a small group of enthusiastic members who can be relied upon not only to attend committees but also to shoulder the enormous amount of work entailed by their decisions. " Teamwork " has always been our watchword—more difficult, perhaps, in a big team than a small one, but even more essential. I feel sure that the grand old Belgrave team spirit will carry us forward to even greater success. On a more personal note, my wife and I wish to express our thanks for the very handsome clock presented to me on my resignation from the Treasurership. I shall value it always, not only for itself, but as a reminder of the many happy years I have spent with the Club. W. G. WEBB. W. G. Webb W. G. WEBB President; formerly Treasurer W. G. WEBB

items.sum: The Hon. Secretary's notes on the season: two Senior National team titles lost in eight days, cross-country championship wins, the London-Brighton Relay hat-trick, a new Junior One Mile Championship with Ernie Musselbrook's cup, the summer fixtures, farewell to Colin Sutton, good wishes to members and sympathy to Teddy Gordon on the loss of his wife.
items.s: The Hon. Secretary—Alf. Harley writes: The Hon. Secretary's notes on the season: two Senior National team titles lost in eight days, cross-country championship wins, the London-Brighton Relay hat-trick, a new Junior One Mile Championship with Ernie Musselbrook's cup, the summer fixtures, farewell to Colin Sutton, good wishes to members and sympathy to Teddy Gordon on the loss of his wife. THE HON. SECRETARY—ALF. HARLEY WRITES: We managed in recent weeks a unique performance in Athletics—that of losing two Senior National team titles in eight days! However, we can console ourselves with the thought that no other athletic club was ever in the position of holding two such titles at the same time. There is profit to be found in defeat and virtue in challenging for a title as well as defending it. They'll come back, giving us redoubled satisfaction; and our younger generation of runners and walkers the thrills and zest in attaining the highest things which wearers of Belgrave colours are entitled to expect. * * * We can still win, of course! Our runners provided winning teams in both Surrey and Middlesex Cross-country Championships. The South of Thames Championship was won, despite barring clauses, for the third time in four years, with Derrick Burfitt leading the field home. The Southern Championship, too, was held, although it must be admitted not so convincingly as on some former occasions; and our walkers have always been prominent in all their racing, and once again retained the Surrey County titles with ease. The London-Brighton Relay gave us a really first class win despite determined opposition from 24 other clubs. We accomplished our second hat-trick of wins in this series of races, and have won this event more times than any other club in the history of nineteen races over the familiar course. This year's race was undoubtedly the most exciting ever, with several clubs taking the lead at various points and more teams than ever before with a possibility of winning, with only ten miles to go. However, Belgrave prevailed as so often before; with Birchfield, Tipton and Reading striving to the end—gallant and sporting opponents as ever. * * * To our already long list of Club Championships has been added yet another—a Junior (under 19) One Mile Championship which will be contested at our Championships Meeting on Saturday, August 6th, for the first time. Happily, a Life Member, Vice President, and former Cross-country Captain, Ernie Musselbrook, has come forward and generously presented a handsome challenge cup for this new championship. He has expressed the hope that this trophy will eventually carry the names of many who will go forward to the Senior ranks and assist the Club to team honours—for Ernie was ever a team man. We gratefully acknowledge his generosity. * * * The only Club Championship without a trophy is the Hop, Step and Jump, and no doubt this will be remedied in due course. It is whispered that a Junior 440 yards Championship may be the next to be considered by the Committee. * * * From the Summer fixture list it will be seen that a very representative range of fixtures has been tabled. We are very grateful to the London Olympiads A.C., for permission to include several events in their programme on June 22nd. It is to be hoped that all members will make the fullest use of the facilities provided and events arranged during the Track Season now upon us. Given the right approach, we can be as effective a force in Track and Field athletics as past years have shown us to be in the realms of Cross-country and Walking. Our Chief Coach and all his assistants, together with the Hon. Secretaries and Captains are anxious to develop and weld our undoubted talent into effective teams; and we have our thoughts and our eyes on the various Relay Championships and on performing creditably in all our Inter-Club fixtures. With the co-operation of every member—determined to do his best for the Club—we can look forward with confidence to the Summer Season. * * * Our good wishes go with Colin Sutton and his wife and Junior Member Robert, on their emigration to Adelaide in far away Australia. We are sorry, indeed, to lose such a fine sporting family and wish them every success in their new environment. Colin has won many Club Championships and assisted the Club to many team wins; and his walking has ranged from 2 to 100 miles. In 1938, he was a member of our winning "Junior", 20 miles; and 50 kilometres R.W.A. Championship teams—a 100 per cent. team member in a 100 per cent. R.W.A. Championship effort, and a unique performance in the world of walking. We shall certainly miss Colin, not only for his abilities but also for his grand sportsmanship and pleasing personality and his great loyalty to the Club. When serving with the R.A.F. in India, he still found time to walk, and finished second in the All-India 50 kilometres Championship—and he still had time to look out for talent for the Club. It is to Colin that we owe the introduction of another grand sportsman and performer—Vern Blowfield—"discovered" by Colin at Service athletic meetings in India and "ear-marked" for Belgrave when still thousands of miles away! All the best to you, Colin and your family; and let's hear from you. Good wishes to Basil Walden, on B.O.A.C. duties in Tripoli; John Briggs and Jack Shields, now studying at Oxford University; to Reg. Ruddick, now qualified for our teams and eager to show his undoubted ability on our behalf; to our Chief Coach, George Clay, recently returned from hospital after an operation; to Harry Thaxter, "Mine Host" at The Sun Inn, Diss, Norfolk, who recently sent greetings to all friends; to E. Thomas Gilbert, who is now serving in H.M.S. Zest; to Don. Arnold, now a corporal in the R.E.M.E.; to our Hon. Secretary, on being elected to the Southern Committee A.A.A., on our nomination, eighteenth of 48 nominations made; to Charlie Smart on getting a Civil Service appointment in this country and so giving us the benefit of his running rather than his Control Commission colleagues and German spectators; to Michael Porter, formerly of Sale Harriers, but now first claim to us on recent Road Race successes. Undoubtedly he will help our teams. We are grateful to Len Marchant who has undertaken the duties of Hon. Press Secretary and does his utmost to ensure that our notes appear in at least ten local newspapers every week. * * * Our profound sympathy goes to Past President Teddy Gordon on the loss of his wife—so well remembered by so many of us. We shall miss Mrs. Gordon at our meetings and functions; and recall with gratitude her many services to the Club in the past. Particularly, one remembers breakfast served on the roadside in the small hours on our Annual All-night Strolls to Brighton; and those many helpful gestures in the early days of the Building Fund. items.sum: Short club notes on members' news: Les. Stokell, Derrick Burfitt, Syd Ring, Fred White, Michael Broadbent, Alan Sexton, Stan Eales, Frank Abberton and David Main, and the Club Stand at the A.A.A. Championships.

items.s: Short club notes on members' news: Les. Stokell, Derrick Burfitt, Syd Ring, Fred White, Michael Broadbent, Alan Sexton, Stan Eales, Frank Abberton and David Main, and the Club Stand at the A.A.A. Championships. Les. Stokell, has now taken a scholastic appointment at a school in Watford and also hopes to have a full season over the country next year. * * Derrick Burfitt, won the R.A.F. C.C. Championship and was third in the Inter-Services race, hopes to be demobbed very shortly. * * * Syd Ring, is out training again and hopes to run in the open long distance road races this season. * * * Fred White, is another who has started training again, and hopes to be running in the Marathon this year. * * * Michael Broadbent, has been playing rugby and finds this very good training and hopes to regain some of his old form on the track this season. * * * Alan Sexton, our Junior A.A.A. 220 yards champion, has been playing for Rosslyn Park First XV, and is being highly spoken of in the "rugger" world. * * * Stan Eales, recently married, was a spectator at the Club 10 miles Championship at Wimbledon. * * * Frank Abberton, also recently married, is now living at Streatham Hill and married life seems to agree with him! * * * David Main, a member of our 1946 winning "National" team, is now running for the East Antrim Harriers in Ireland, and hopes to be over here during the Summer. * * * There will be the usual "Club" Stand at the A.A.A. Championships on Saturday, July 16th, at the White City, seats numbered and reserved at 3s. 6d. each. Members wishing to avail themselves of this privilege should advise Frank Webb, 50, Longford Avenue, Southall, including CASH with order. The "Supporters Club," after a most successful winter season, has now closed down until the autumn, when new members will be welcomed by Les Cohen from whom full particulars may be obtained. * * * Jack Shotter, who has recently returned from India, is now in regular training at Belgrave Hall. * * * Congratulations to Tom Cotton and his wife upon the latest addition to their family. These notes may be a little behind times but I'm sure Patricia will not mind. * * * All Ernie Duffett's many friends will be pleased to know that his wife who has been in hospital for a major operation, is now back home and is very much better. * * * Frank Abberton, Bill Lucas and Len Marchant, having been selected by Surrey County for the Inter Counties Championship at Manchester, finished 41st, 44th and 80th respectively. * * * Our best wishes to Tom Fifield who has migrated to South Africa. * * * Bernard Eglinton, our Derby member, a sergeant in the R.A.F., writes from Ismailia (Egypt) that he is missing Wimbledon Common and the comradeship of Belgrave Hall. He sends his best wishes to ALL. * * * Arthur Allen, now in the Artillery, sends greetings from Plymouth where he is keeping fit as a P.T. Instructor. * * * Tony Whincup has followed his wife to Crewe where they are now settling down. He has joined a local club but is not too happy about it. Thanks a lot Tony for the telegram of best wishes for the "National." * * * Our thanks are due to Edward Greenwood for his assistance in taking out a youth's pack at Belgrave Hall each Saturday afternoon. This is a little known service performed. * * * We must also thank Micky Pyer for all his work amongst the "youths," the results of which will be forthcoming in the future. * * * Frank Elson is, we regret to report, again very ill and waiting to go into hospital for another operation. All his many friends will wish him a speedy recovery. * * * Our thanks to George Atkinson and Syd Roberts for getting the B.N.L. into circulation again. * * * Bob Readman won the Met. Police 10 miles Walking Championship at Imber Court on February 24th, and a month later was second in the National Police Championship. * * * Harry Churcher won the London Business Houses 7 miles Walking Championship on January 8th, at Southgate, and R. D. McMullen was second. * * * Jack Rutland was third in the British Workers 10 miles Walking Championship at Enfield on February 19th, in 83m. 5s.; McMullen was fourth and J. H. Robins fifth. Martin Williamson was selected to run for Cambridge University in the Mile Relay against Oxford, in the Universities Relay Meeting and he also represented Cambridge University in the Annual Oxford and Cambridge Track Meet at the White City in March. At Cambridge on December 4th he very ably led home Cambridge "B" team to an overwhelming victory over Oxford "B." * * * They do things slightly differently on the Continent than we do here in England. Our war-time member, Etienne Gailly (Steve) and Belgium Olympic Marathon hero has been awarded the annual Grand Prix d'honneur for the outstanding athlete of the year 1948; and at Brussels he was awarded the annual "Trophie National du Merite Sportif," chosen on account of his Olympic Marathon performance. He was also placed fourth in a poll recently organised by Belgium's leading sports daily to find the most popular athlete for the year. * * * Albert Frost was fifth in the Civil Service 5 miles Championship at Addington. * * * Recent R.W.A. appointments include Harold King, Alf Harley and Charles Warren as Judges, Syd Roberts as Supplementary Judge and Dick Savage as Timekeeper. * * * Bert Ellsey has also been re-appointed delegate from the Southern Counties Cross Country Association to the Southern Committee A.A.A. and also been re-elected a Vice President of the Surrey County A.A.A. * * * Other recent appointments to the Surrey County A.A.A. are Harry Parker and Jack Chapple as Vice Presidents and Joe Coleman, Dick Savage and Charlie Jones elected to the Committee. * * * Congratulations to our old friends the "Poly" on their third place in the "Southern," ably helped by our own Poly member, Jimmy Wood, who was 23rd. Ron Hughes, who was with us during the war, was an excellent fifth and Rene Howell was 160th. * * * Congratulations also to Sutton Harriers on their splendid win in the "National." In a field of nearly 450 runners they scored 128 points, 121 in front of the second team, Reading. * * * Geoff. Pearson was sixth in the Inter-Banks Championship over 4½ miles at Hayes (Kent), and third in the Westminster Bank 5 miles Championship. * * * Bill Lucas was second in the Insurance Championship over 5 miles at Coulsdon. Incidentally, he has been asked to hold himself in readiness for the British Empire Games in New Zealand in 1950. * * * Amongst his other achievements during this winter season, Eddie Short was fourth in the London University Championship, over 4¾ miles at Roehampton. Fourth in the Universities Athletic Union 7 miles Championship and second in the Inter University match against Cambridge University. He represented the English Universities against Scottish Universities, when he finished dead heat first with three other team mates. * * * Len Marchant won the London Business Houses Championship over 5 miles at Wimbledon. * * * Bert Clayton won the Hants County 10 mile walk Championship on January 29th at Eastleigh, in 85m. 45s.; with Percy Wright 4th in 90m. 49s. items.s: Hon. Treasurer's Notes The Hon. Treasurer acknowledges donations to club funds, explains when subscriptions fall due and the exemption for members in H.M. Forces, and asks for changes of address. HON. TREASURER'S NOTES The following donations to general club funds have been received during the past six months from the following members, and I wish to express the thanks of the committee for their generosity:—Messrs. G. A. Atkinson, O. Horwood, £2 2s.; J. G. Coleman, T. H. Cotton, T. C. Jones, £1; F. S. Bradnum, 11s.; L. J. Cohen, A. A. Harley, H. E. Footer, A. E. Taylor, F. R. Webb, 10s.; E. Musselbrook, 5s. These are additional to donations given by various members to the Open Walk Prize Fund, and the Children's Party Fund. * * * Many members seem unaware that Club Subscriptions become due in September of each year, and cover the period up to the following September. A member who joins at any time after September pays a full year's subscription, but his next subscription becomes due the following September. It will assist me considerably if subscriptions are paid promptly, without waiting for a reminder. * * * It may not be generally known that the Committee have ruled that members serving in H.M. Forces under the National Service Act may be excused payment of their subscriptions, but it is essential that such members should advise the Hon. Treasurer that they wish to take advantage of this concession. If no communication is received we have no means of knowing the member is entitled to be excused payment. * * * One other small but important matter, do please keep the Hon. Secretary or Hon. Treasurer informed of all changes of address, and so save the bother of having communications returned "Not known." G. A. Atkinson G. A. Atkinson donation £2 2s. O. Horwood O. Horwood donation £2 2s. CLUB "HANDICAPS" Are you a handicap or an asset to the Club? Excluding Life members and members serving with Services, we have a membership of about 650. Of this number nearly 300 have paid their subscriptions for the current year, whilst of the remainder, 215 have paid for last year, leaving nearly 150 who have not paid anything since the Club year 1946-7 or earlier. If you are in arrears with your subscription please send a remittance straight away to the Hon. Treasurer, and so save him the time, and the Club the expense, of sending a reminder to you.
