items.s: The "Overseas" Trophy—Percy Wright says: Percy Wright reports that the "Overseas" Trophy fund raised from wartime "Airgraphs" stands at £6 19s. 6d. and appeals to members who served overseas to subscribe so a cup can be bought. THE "OVERSEAS" TROPHY—PERCY WRIGHT SAYS: Remember it? We planned it for after the war with the money that we made on those "Airgraphs" you chaps sent me. Unfortunately, the man that bought the "Airgraphs" died and this source of income died with him. We had, however, succeeded in getting quite a tidy sum—£6 19s. 6d., to be exact. I had hoped to plan something else to raise the money to a sufficient sum to purchase a suitable trophy, but my present distance from the Club quarters is not convenient. It has been suggested to me that I make an appeal to all those who served overseas and would like to see the idea of the "Overseas" Cup materialise to send along a subscription. Well, lads! what about it? Send your cheque, postal order or stamp, either to me or to the Hon. Treasurer, not forgetting to mention what it is for. We should also be pleased to have any suggestions on how the trophy shall be awarded. This appeal is addressed to all Club members who served overseas and not only the Walkers. 34, Elgar Road, Sholing, Southampton. Percy Wright PERCY WRIGHT PERCY WRIGHT Sholing Southampton

items.s: Walking Notes Syd Roberts reviews the walkers' winter season: the club 5 miles Handicap, the Highgate, Enfield, Belgrave, Cambridge Harriers and Met. Police Opens, and the Horwood Cup Race. WALKING NOTES By SYD ROBERTS The winter season opened with our usual 5 miles Handicap, with a match against the Police in conjunction. In all, 40 Walkers started, including 25 of our members, a promising start for the new season. In the absence of Harry Churcher, Bob McMullen led the field, followed by Bob Readman and Smith of the Police. F. Tasker, rapidly improving, won the Handicap, with Brian Shepherd second and Don Heath third. In the first Open of the Season, Highgate Harriers 7, at Parliament Hill Fields, we entered three teams, but neither Harry Churcher or Joe Coleman were amongst the competitors and with Jack Rutland nowhere near his last year's form, we had to be content with third scratch team. A fortnight later came the Enfield Open and although it was the same day as the Club Dinner, this did not deter the majority of our Walkers from making the long journey to Enfield for the race and back to Clapham for the dinner. This race was the beginning of a winning sequence, practically all our men walking up to form. Harry Churcher soon set up a good lead and remained unchallenged. In addition, we took scratch team honours with the "B" and "A" teams second and third respectively in the Handicap and George Oliver second in the Individual Handicap. Next came our own Open with, as usual, the biggest entry of the season. Although a little below last year's total of 248, there was an almost total absence of provincial entries due, no doubt, to the ever increasing cost of travelling. The weather, however, was not very kind to us and as a result of a very dense fog a number of competitors were unable to reach Wimbledon. Despite the conditions, 182 Walkers faced the starter, and once again Harry Churcher led throughout. Backed up by McMullen, Readman and East, we succeeded in retaining the "Berman" Trophy. Our "B" team once again finished second in the Team Handicap and Len Fletcher, proving he can still show some of them the way round, finished fourteenth and was awarded the prize for the first unplaced member. Our thanks are again due to those loyal members who contributed to the prize fund and also to the large number of officials who gave such valuable assistance under very trying conditions. A fortnight later we held the Horwood Cup Race. A field of 22 juniors lined up for the start and once again Bert East led them home, with George Bentley second and Pat Sapcote third. Charlie Speechley, still having a go, won the Handicap, with George Atkinson second and Joe Scammell third. On the same day a Novices 3 miles race resulted in a win for E. Evans, one of our new Walkers. The following week our Walkers travelled to Bexley Heath for the Cambridge Harriers Open and continued our winning sequence in the scratch race with Harry Churcher leading the team home. Once again the "B" team were second in the Team Handicap. With the new year, came the Met. Police Open at Imber Court. In a field of over 200 starters, Harry Churcher soon took the lead on this very fast course and the scratch team added yet one more to their list of Open wins, this time Charlie Churcher getting his first place in the winning team. With the continued run of Handicap placings our teams were unable to get in the first three. The following Saturday, we held our 10 miles Club Championship, which, needless to say, was once again won by the invincible Harry, with Bob McMullen second and evergreen Bob Readman third. Alan Robins, the first "junior" to finish, showed a marked improvement and was placed fifth. A match in conjunction resulted in the Police being beaten by 55 points. And so we come to the Junior Championship at Enfield on February 5th. Although we had a reasonably good team it was generally thought that competition would be keen between Cambridge Harriers, Highgate Harriers and ourselves, and not much was known of the strength of Midland and Northern Clubs. Sheffield, however, proved to be very strong and their scoring four finished in the first dozen. Coleman of Highgate and Long of Cambridge, having been ruled out of their respective teams by the referee, we were given second place with 48 points. Unfortunately for us this was later reversed by the A.A.A. Southern Committee, the revised placings being Highgate second, 52 points, Cambridge third, 53 points, Belgrave fourth, 56 points. Alan Robins again walked exceptionally well to lead the team home with Bert East, George Bentley and Pat Sapcote supporting him. George Oliver, who had been off form recently, was relegated to the "B" Team, but was fifth club man to finish. In the Surrey Championship we once again secured double honours, Harry Churcher leading the team in his usual style, followed by Charlie, Mac and Bert East. Charlie was again selected as Team Captain for the County, the other three also being members of the team with Syd James as reserve, for the Inter Counties Championship at Leicester. Our Cadogan members in the Middlesex Championship did not fare so well, with the exception of Bob Readman who finished second to Jim Morris, the team being fourth. Bob was selected to represent Middlesex and Alan Robins, finishing fourth in the Kent Championship the same day was selected to represent that county. And so to Leicester for the National 10. Keen competition was once again expected from Highgate and Cambridge, with little known of Sheffield apart from their "Junior" win. Harry Churcher and Allen of Sheffield set the pace from the start, but unfortunately at about 3½ miles Harry failed to please one of the Northern judges and was disqualified. This left Sheffield in a very strong position and at 6½ miles they had three men in the first seven with a total score of 31 points. Our first four were well placed at 6, 8, 9 and 19, 11 points behind Sheffield, with Charlie Churcher rapidly moving up. Jack Rutland, however, was having some trouble and slowed up slightly. Highgate occupying fourth, fifth, sixteenth and twenty-fourth positions were a few points behind us. Towards the last mile, Mac showed signs of tiring and whilst Charlie moved up still further, eventually overtaking Bob Readman, Mac slipped back to tenth position. Jack Rutland clung on desperately, maintaining his position to the finish, but with one or two in the first twenty dropping back, Highgate improved their third and fourth positions gaining seven points against our loss of one. Sheffield also lost a few points over the last stages, but this did not prevent them maintaining a clear lead, and with L. Allen nearly two minutes in front of Jim Morris, they took double honours, with Highgate in second place, beating us by one point. Congratulations to Bob Readman in getting seventh place and thus qualifying for Club Honours Badge. Bob was also a member of the winning team in the Inter Counties Championship which was won by Middlesex. items.label: No. 105
items.h: A Review of the Cross Country Season
items.sum: Ernie Duffett reviews Belgrave's 1948-49 cross-country season: wins in the Surrey, Middlesex (as Cadogan A.C.), South of Thames and Southern championships, but a poor showing in the National at Birmingham.
items.s: A Review of the Cross Country Season Ernie Duffett reviews Belgrave's 1948-49 cross-country season: wins in the Surrey, Middlesex (as Cadogan A.C.), South of Thames and Southern championships, but a poor showing in the National at Birmingham. Although naturally hoping to do as well as last season, when we cleared the board so far as the major championships went I think that apart from our dismal showing in the "National" race, that our ruuners can be said to have done well throughout the season. We started by failing to secure a place in the South of Thames "Junior," but this was due more to the selection of our teams than to the failure of our runners. Eric Herbert, who was our second man home in 15th position, had been put in the "B" team and we had to go back to 57th for our fourth scoring "A" team runner. Even so we only lost third place by 1 point, but with Eric Herbert in our "A" team we should have been an easy second to Surrey A.C., who won the race with the low score of 30 points. We won both the Surrey County and Middlesex County events, the latter by reason of our members who ran for their second-claim club, Cadogan A.C. Frank Abberton was the individual winner of the Surrey race and Derrick Burfitt only failed by a couple of yards to repeat this performance in the Middlesex event. In the South of Thames 7 miles Championship at Horsham, we repeated our win of last season and have now won this race three times in the last four years. As the winning six scorers are barred from competing again, it will be seen the considerable strength which we have, and it is this that makes us all the more optimistic about the future. In addition to again winning the "Dewar" Shield we also won the "Colman" Cup awarded to the club which has the lowest score for its complete team of 12 runners, and indeed our score for 12 men was lower than some clubs had for their team of six counters. The Southern race was held at Camberley and with a field of over 350 runners, team scoring was naturally high. Even so, our winning total of 183 points was the highest ever in the history of this event, so I think the best that can be said was that we were the best of a poor lot! Here again we won the "Oddling-Smee" Cup for finishing our complete team before any other Surrey club, and we actually had 11 men in the first 96 scoring places, which in such a large field is excellent running. So to the "National" at Birmingham and although we were not too optimistic we certainly expected at least to get a place, and so continue our unbroken list of placings in this event since our initial third place in 1933. There was a huge field of 449 runners and it does seem as if some qualifying rule should apply to clubs entering this event as some of the competitors were hopelessly outclassed and a large number were lapped. We had some consolation in winning the "Charles Otway" Cup, awarded to the first club, outside the placed teams, to finish its team of 9 men, but hope that next year we shall once again be up to the front and fighting it out with the Sutton lads, who will be hard to displace from their positions as champions. items.s: South of Thames "Junior" Team Race Report of the South of Thames Junior cross-country team race at Farningham, where Belgrave's "A" team was fourth, one point off third, with the placings of the A, B and C teams. Held at Farningham on November 6th over a rather tough 5 miles course and with an entry of 50 teams, a record for the race, a field of 316 runners faced the starter. We were drawn on the outside but after the initial breakaway Archie Bedford was seen to be lying second and Eddie Short was also well up. At the half-distance the latter was in fourth place but there was no sign of Archie, and it later transpired that he had dropped out owing to shoe trouble at about 2 miles, which was certainly very bad luck for his team-mates. Eric Herbert was our second man but running for "B" team. This was won easily by Surrey A.C., who had a strong four and they all ran well. The Portsmouth R.N. boys surprised many by gaining second place and Aylesford Paper Mills just pipped our "A" team by 1 point for third place. Eddie Short was rather unlucky in just missing a place, he finished 4th in last year's race, and Mike Heard and Arthur Bruce both did well in such a large field. Eric Herbert and George Durrant both upset the team selectors by their forward running, but these things have happened before and no doubt will occur again. items.sum: Report of the 50th South of Thames cross-country championship at Horsham, won by Derrick Burfitt from Peter Curry, with Belgrave first team and winners of the Colman Cup.
items.s: South of Thames Championship Report of the 50th South of Thames cross-country championship at Horsham, won by Derrick Burfitt from Peter Curry, with Belgrave first team and winners of the Colman Cup. The 50th annual cross-country championship was held at Horsham on February 12th, over a 7½ miles course. A field of 187 runners turned out and the course arrangements and loud speakers for the benefit of the spectators were very good, and quite up to "National" standard. Over the first small lap Peter Curry, the Olympic Games steeplechase representative was in the lead closely followed by Derrick Burfitt. On completion of the first big lap, Curry and Burfitt had drawn away from the rest of the field and were running stride for stride. When they came in sight of the finish, however, Derrick was well in front and he won in fine style in the good time of 44 mins. 13 secs. with Curry clocking 44.44 in second place. Our lads had gradually been working their way through the field with Len Marchant always up with the leading bunch, and eventually Mike Heard was 11th with Jack Brown 13th and George Durrant 14th, which was a very good show on their part. J. McDonald was our sixth man in 28th position and Len Adams 38th and Lou Bush 40th gave good support. With such forward running we easily won the "Colman" Cup for the first club to finish their complete team of 12 men, and Ken England is to be complimented on finishing the course after having a bad time. items.s: Southern Counties C.C. Championships Report of the Southern Counties cross-country championships at Sandhurst, where Belgrave retained the senior team title and the Oddling-Smee Cup, with Youths, Junior and Senior placings. These were held at the Royal Military Academy, Sandhurst, on February 26th, and the dressing arrangements were first class. A field of over 350 runners turned out for the Senior 10 miles race, and after a very fast start across the playing fields, the field then had to do 4 laps out in the country which consisted of running through woods with some steep inclines included. Ted Stimpson was always well up with the first dozen runners, but Vern Blowfield was suffering with shoe trouble and was gradually dropping back while Len Herbert and Marchant were striving to hold their places, but things did not look too good for our prospects of retaining our title as Southern champions. However, on the final lap, Blowfield started to pick up again and Steve Charlton and Tom Carter were also coming through the field to consolidate our scoring positions. Even so, with our six men in 46 we were not too optimistic and were frankly surprised when told that we had won the team race once again. We also retained the "Oddling-Smee" Cup awarded to the first Surrey club to finish their 12 men, and so brought the trophies back home again for the second successive year. In the Youths race Michael Stearman ran well to finish 22nd, but the rest of our boys lacked racing experience. The Junior race saw Eddie Short having his usual bad luck in finishing 4th, he must be getting used to this position now, and Arthur Bruce was 47th, but here again they lacked support. items.sum: Report of the English (National) cross-country championships at Bromford Bridge, Birmingham, where Belgrave lost their title to Sutton Harriers and finished sixth, with the club's Youths, Junior and Senior placings.
items.s: English Cross Country Championships Report of the English (National) cross-country championships at Bromford Bridge, Birmingham, where Belgrave lost their title to Sutton Harriers and finished sixth, with the club's Youths, Junior and Senior placings. On March 12th we journeyed to Birmingham for the "National," held on the Bromford Bridge Racecourse, although the runners actually ran outside the course, which included a cinder path, a mud splash and a descent something like a shute used at a swimming bath. As the seniors had to do 4 laps of this gruelling course the spectators were given a good view of the racing, but what the runners thought is another matter. On the first small lap of the senior race Vern Blowfield was up to the front with Aaron, the eventual winner, but could not hold his position and gradually fell back. Our other men were well placed to begin with but as each lap came round, with the exception of Steve Charlton, they seemed to go further and further back while our most dangerous rivals, Sutton Harriers, had their men well up and going forward all the time. We soon realised that we had lost our title of "National" champions, but must say that the Sutton lads deserved their win and are indeed worthy champions. Vern Blowfield was our first man home, 18th, and Steve Charlton did well in being 58th, and after him our next four men packed well but were, of course, too far back to stand a chance of getting placed in the team race. However, we need not be too discouraged, as we have some good youngsters coming along to take the older men's places, and surely our chaps cannot run so bad next year, or at least, we hope not. In the Junior race Eddie Short again ran well and although having a couple of falls down the "shute," he was our first man home in 13th place. C. W. Walker, the winner of our recent road race for Novices, did well in his first "open" race to finish in 34th position, but we missed the services of Arthur Bruce, who could not get leave from his unit. items.s: Surrey (Senior) Cross Country Championship Len Marchant's report of the Surrey senior cross-country championship at Earlwood, won by Frank Abberton with Belgrave first team, followed by the County Junior race and Ernie Duffett's note on the County Youths' race at Addington. As was the case with most of the counties on New Year's Day, Surrey held their championship under very trying climatic conditions. The 7½ miles course at Earlwood was completely waterlogged owing to the very heavy rain, this coupled with a strong, bitterly cold wind caused the majority to "swear" once again that "it's a mug's game!" Those who were fortunate enough to get in front of the field over the first mile stayed there, and during the whole race the leading men remained the same, Frank Abberton, Bowering (S.L.H.) and Barry (H.H.H.) fighting for first place, Bill Lucas and Marchant being a few places further back. In the final check-up it was found that George Durrant had run exceptionally well to finish 15th. Frank Abberton ran exceptionally well to win such a gruelling race after having to battle all the way. Len Herbert did not find the going to his liking and finished no nearer than 19th closely followed by our Poly member, Jimmy Wood, who had ran steadily throughout to finish 23rd. This is our 14th win in this championship. 1, F. Abberton, 44.1; 7, W. Lucas, 45.13; 8, Marchant, 45.21; 15, Durrant, 46.15; 19, L. Herbert, 46,45; 23, Wood; 47.0; 26, Williamson, 47.48; 28, Carter, 47.54; 32, Bush, 48.21; 37, C. Abberton, 48.57; 44, Davies, 49.28; Towndrow, 49.37. Result: 1, Belgrave, 73 pts.; 2, S.L.H., 79 pts. * * * The County Junior Race over 5 miles was held immediately preceding the senior race and resulted in our team being placed 4th with a points total of 62 for four runners, against 27 points of the winners. Our team positions were:— 2, E. Short, 29.59; 11, L. Adams, 31.55; 23, S. Brooks, 34.15; 26, C. Collins, 35.8; 29, R. Garwood, 35.40; 32, J. Lacey, 36.49; 33, F. Pettitt, 36.56. * * * Ernie Duffett says:— The County Youths' Race was held at Addington December 4th, and we fielded a full team of 8 men with 4 to score. M. J. Stearman, our Surrey Youths' 1 mile champion, ran well in his first race over the country, to finish third to E. L. Brown (Mitcham A.C.) and D. A. G. Pirie (S.L.H.). Our other placings were: 37, B. L. Chitty; 44, M. J. Hazel; 49, R. J. Mitchell; 52, J. K. Hill; 55, P. A. Smith; 59, R. A. Butt; 62, D. Briggs. We were placed 8th in the team race, and as our lads were rather on the young side for such a heavy course, with more racing experience we can look forward to better results under Micky Pyer's tuition. items.sum: Harry Shields reports on the Middlesex county cross-country championship at Trent Park, won as a team by Cadogan A.C. (a team of Belgravians), with Derrick Burfitt second by one second to Olney.
items.s: Middlesex County Championship, Trent Park, January 1st Harry Shields reports on the Middlesex county cross-country championship at Trent Park, won as a team by Cadogan A.C. (a team of Belgravians), with Derrick Burfitt second by one second to Olney. Cadogan A.C. were represented by a full team of Belgravians and the race was held in a howling gale over a three lap course totalling 7½ miles. The venue is that over which it is proposed to hold the 1950 "National" and is a good sporting course of undulating grassland. Our team got away to a good start and quickly showed to advantage with Derrick Burfitt and Vern Blowfield among the leaders. Derrick and Olney (T.V.H.) soon sorted themselves out and together fighting all the way Olney eventually won on the tape by taking the "proverbial deep breath," the timekeepers giving Olney one second's advantage. The team won with a score of 85 pts., the second team being another 45 pts. behind. items.s: "Blackstaffe Shield" Race Report and full result of the club's 7 miles cross-country championship for the Blackstaffe Shield on December 11th, won by Len Herbert, with L. Bush winning the handicap. Our 7 Miles Cross Country Championship was held on December 11th, and a record field of 55 runners faced the starter, of whom 48 finished. At the half-distance Ted Stimpson was in the lead followed by Len Herbert and George Lucas, but when the runners came in sight of the finish Len Herbert was in front and running strongly. The other positions were unchanged except that Mike Heard was hot on the heels of George Lucas, followed by Arthur Bruce and Martin Williamson, and it is pleasing to see these youngsters giving the senior members such a strong challenge. Jimmy Wood and Rene Howell (our Poly members) were also in the field and Bert Footer surprised a few by his forward running. L. Bush deservedly won the handicap while George Durrant continued his improved form to gain second place with Eric Bishop beating his brother, Alan, for third prize. items.sum: Report and full result of the club's 10 miles cross-country championship for the Macher Shield on January 29th, won by Vic Blowfield, with J. McDonald winning the handicap and a note of the 1928 placings.
items.s: "Macher" Shield Race Report and full result of the club's 10 miles cross-country championship for the Macher Shield on January 29th, won by Vic Blowfield, with J. McDonald winning the handicap and a note of the 1928 placings. The 10 Miles Cross Country Championship for the "Macher" Shield was held on January 29th. It was a glorious afternoon and a field of 45 faced the starter, Albert Macher, the eldest son of the donor. At the half-distance Vic Blowfield and Frank Abberton were together in the lead with Bill Lucas and Len Marchant fairly handy, but the rest of the field were already well strung out. When they came in sight of the finish Blowfield was in front with Frank Abberton still second, but Len Marchant had come through to third place. There was rather a gap after the first three home but the rest of the field then arrived at regular intervals with Tom Carter and Stan Davies having a desperate sprint to the finishing line, which Tom won by inches. When the handicap had been worked out it was found that J. McDonald was the winner and he certainly ran well in his usual determined style and there was a dead heat for second place between Jack Brown and "Ginger" Charlton, which the latter won on the toss of a coin with Brown taking third prize. There was a good crowd present and we were pleased to see our old club champion, Arthur Clark, who won this race twice, and as a matter of interest the 1928 placings were: 1, A. Clark; 2, E. A. Duffett; 3, A. D. Pyer; 4, W. G. Webb; 5, H. E. Footer; and we are pleased to see that four of the above are still very much with the club after 21 years have gone by. * Denotes dead heat. items.s: Five Miles Road Race Report and full result of the club's five miles road race at Belgrave Hall on March 19th, where the first two went off course and the handicap went to Albert Frost. FIVE MILES ROAD RACE. Held at Belgrave Hall on March 19th, and a field of 54 runners faced the starter, who was our old club champion and ex-Empire Games 6 miles champion, Arthur (Nutty) Penny. Len Marchant set a fast pace round the first small lap and a bunch of about eight runners were well up with him. When they came in sight again Vernon Blowfield was in the lead with Jack Brown running stride for stride with him, and then, unfortunately, they went slightly off the course, and so came home well in front of the rest of the field. Ted Stimpson, who was third, kept to the correct road and the rest of the field followed him, so it was decided to ignore the first two runners' placings in the handicap result. This resulted in a win for Albert Frost, who had run well above his recent form, and Alf Taylor took second prize by 1 sec. from George Chantler. The first nine home all completed the course, which is reckoned to be over the stipulated distance, in under 30 mins., and these times augured well for our chances of winning the London to Brighton Relay for the third successive year. items.s: Inter-Club Matches Reports of a senior and junior match against Mitcham A.C. at Roehampton and a "B" team match against Old Croydonians A.C. at Belgrave Hall. INTER-CLUB MATCHES. On November 13th we visited the Mitcham A.C. quarters at Roehampton for a senior and a junior match. The senior race was won by Len Marchant, and of the first six home five were " Bels." Mitcham, however, provided the first three in the junior race and beat us by 19 pts. to 49 pts. Leading positions in the senior match were: 1, L. M. Marchant, 31.56; 2, W. E. Lucas, 32.3; 3, R. F. items.s: Novices Road Race Report and result of a 3 miles road race for unattached novices and Malden youth clubs held from Belgrave Hall on December 11th, won by C. W. Walker. NOVICES ROAD RACE. On December 11th we held a 3 miles road race open to Unattached Novices from Belgrave Hall, and also in conjunction we held a race open to the Youth Clubs of Malden. items.sum: Report and results of the club's Boxing Day meeting on Tooting Common track: 100 yards, 3 miles walk, 2 miles run and weight put handicaps.
items.s: Boxing Day Meeting Report and results of the club's Boxing Day meeting on Tooting Common track: 100 yards, 3 miles walk, 2 miles run and weight put handicaps. BOXING DAY MEETING. Held at Tooting Common track with a white frost showing everywhere, and as a result the track was bone hard. Entries in the sprint were not too good but six heats with two or more runners in each were made up, and with six runners in the final a good race was seen. G. S. Robinson, one of our promising junior sprinters, was first with another junior in R. B. Thomas second, and John Briggs now demobbed and up at Oxford University gained third place, with Alan Sexton, our Junior A.A.A. 220 yards champion, a close fourth. The Walk was won by Percy Wilson with 5.45 start, and Harry Churcher walked well from the scartch mark to gain second place. A new member in S. James, off 4.45, was third. A good field was seen in the 2 miles run and Eric Bishop, off 260 yds., was a good winner with Martin Williamson, off 180, second, and Lou Bush, off 300 yds., third. Derrick Burfitt ran well, off a back mark, to run through to sixth position, and looks to be in for a good season over the country. 100 Yards (heat winners): R. B. Thomas (7); A. D. Sexton (1); P. V. items.h: Cambridge University at Belgrave Hall on January 22nd
items.sum: Bill Lucas and Alf Taylor report a "B" team match against Cambridge University (with Kent A.C.) over the club 7 miles course, won by Cambridge; the report calls Martin Williamson "our own" while the result marks him (C).
items.s: Cambridge University at Belgrave Hall on January 22nd Bill Lucas and Alf Taylor report a "B" team match against Cambridge University (with Kent A.C.) over the club 7 miles course, won by Cambridge; the report calls Martin Williamson "our own" while the result marks him (C). CAMBRIDGE UNIVERSITY AT BELGRAVE HALL ON JANUARY 22nd. Bill Lucas and Alf Taylor writes:— This match, which was run over the Club 7 miles course in ideal conditions, was designated as a "B" team fixture, but it soon became apparent that more than a "B" team was needed to defeat the Cambridge runners, which included three men who participated in this year's Varsity race, ably backed by their second strings. Len Marchant set a fast pace from the start and quickly gained a 30 yds. lead, which was not lost until the beginning of the second lap when Bill Lucas with Gorton and Palmer, of Cambridge, in close attendance, took up the running. This order was maintained until the Windmill when the two Cambridge boys went away together from Lucas to win by 16 secs. in the good time of 39.33, which incidentally had rarely been beaten in our own club championships over this same course. As Cambridge had their scoring six in the first nine places, including our own Martin Williamson, who was 5th, they finished easy winners with 30 pts. against 57 pts. by Belgrave. It was good to see Minahan racing again after a long lapse through injury and it is hoped that he will be able to continue his training. Good performances were put up by Adams (11th), England (12th) and Chantler (14th) to complete our scoring six. Kent A.C. also joined in this match, their first runner being Gravely in the 8th position. Result:—1, Gorton and Palmer (C), 39.33; 3, W. Lucas (B), 39.49; 4, Marchant (B), 40.4; M. items.s: Thames Valley Harriers Road Relay Report and leg times of the Thames Valley Harriers road relay at Cranford on March 26th, won by Birchfield, with Belgrave "B" third and "A" fourth. THAMES VALLEY HARRIERS ROAD RELAY. Held on March 26th, at Cranford, and we had entered five teams, although our National team men were having a rest from competitive racing. Birchfield had sent down a useful four runners and they held off all challenges to win a good race. Our "A" and "B" teams had been having a battle royal in 2nd and 3rd positions, but Alec Olney on the last "leg," put up a really smashing performance to clock 23.4 for the journey of about 4½ miles, and took his club into second place. Our "B" team finished third with our "A" team fourth, and as there were four sets of prizes, our lads were well satisfied with the result of their efforts. Eddie Short ran the best of our men with Bill Lucas showing next best time and Steve Charlton and Tom Carter, despite a fall over a bicycle during his "leg," also ran well. It was unfortunate that our "D" team failed to close in owing to being a runner short and it is a pity that runners do not advise someone if they find they cannot turn out for a race. items.s: The Track Season for 1949 Ernie Duffett sets out the club's 1949 track fixtures and championships and asks for entries to be sent to him. THE TRACK SEASON FOR 1949. Ernie Duffett writes:— Your Committee have arranged a full list of fixtures for both Senior and Junior members, and there are also a number of "B" team matches for the lesser lights. We open our track season on May 7th with a club meeting at Tooting, and we then have matches arranged for each Saturday in May. The County Championships are on June 4th, with Surrey at Motspur Park and the Middlesex at Southall. On the Whit Monday, Surrey County are holding their Junior 4 x 110 yds. relay and the Senior Mile Medley relay at the "Charlotteville" meeting at Guildford, which is a very good grass track. June 18th is the "Kinnaid" meeting at Chiswick with Poly Marathon race from Windsor in conjunction, and we have decided to again hold our Club Marathon Championship for the "A. F. Mitchell" Shield on the result of this race. On June 22nd, at Tooting, we are holding our 3 miles track championship, by kind permission of the London Olympiades A.C., who have the track booked for this evening. June 25th is Southern Championship Day and this year they are being held at the Hove Stadium track. On July 9th there are the Southern Junior Championships at Cambridge and although this is rather far from town we hope as many of our Juniors as possible will enter. The A.A.A. Championships are on July 15th and 16th at the White City, and they are also holding the Junior Relay Championship in conjunction with the Senior events. On July 30th the A.A.A. Junior Championships are being held at Birmingham on the Birchfield Harriers track at Perry Barr. Club Championship Dap is August 6th at Tooting, and a new addition to our list of championships at a 1 mile for Juniors under 19, for the "Musselbrook" Cup. Entries for all events should be sent in at least a week beforehand and only members entered on the programme will be allowed to compete. The Surrey County Youths Championships are at Tooting on September 10th, and the following Saturday at the same track we hold our final track meeting of the 1949 season. There are handicap events to suit all ages, also a 1 mile race for Unattached Novices, so if any of your friends fancy themselves as a runner, don't forget to bring them along on that day. All entries for running events should be sent to me at the following address, a card will do, as you can pay the entry fee on the day. 57, Harcourt Road, Thornton Heath. items.sum: Terry Bateman reviews the club's field events prospects for the coming season event by event and urges members to train and support the coming meetings.
items.s: Field Events Gossip Terry Bateman reviews the club's field events prospects for the coming season event by event and urges members to train and support the coming meetings. FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP. Terry Bateman writes:— This coming season, it is hoped, the Club will improve so that we shall at least attain if not exceed our pre-war standard in Field Events. We have a number of new members to support this hope. "Steve" Gibson, in the High Jump, has already achieved quite good performances with "the Scissors" style. All the winter he has been gradually evolving the "Western Roll" technique and before the end of the season should show improved performances. With Dick Negus back in training, and, we hope, back to his form of two years ago, we should be quite strong in this event. We hope also to have the assistance of John Boxall now that his examinations are nearly at an end. Unfortunately, our chance of having Wilf Anderson, our Club Champion, out are practically nil as he is on a tour of duty in Germany with the R.A.F. "Steve" Gibson, Les Christmas and Stan Botwright will be our main hopes in the Long Jump, but it would be good to see Geoff Wood taking part in this event more often as it is felt he has good possibilities. Geoff Wood and Les Christmas, together with Bert Machell, will be our Hop, Step and Jump men. Geoff Wood should get near A.A.A. Standard, and Les Christmas with more training getting over 40 feet. In the heavy events we do not seem to have any new blood. Jock Mackenzie in the Discus should again show improvement and will be backed up by Sid Jones and Bill Sutton. Sid and Bill will be our Shot Putters, but Jock Mackenzie and Les Christmas have possibilities if they only get down to training. There is a need for more men in both these events and some of those heavyweights who find running a bit too arduous might think seriously of taking up either or both events. In the Javelin we hope to have the assistance of the two old stalwarts. Charlie Melchior and George Powell. However, it is to Alan Dunn, Geoff Jarvis, Arthur Allen and Terry Bateman we look for improved performances and from at least one, distances approaching, even if not beating those achieved by the old stalwarts in previous years. Geoff Jarvis, who is in the R.A.F., is also quite a good hurdler both over the High and 440 yds. distances. We hope he will be able to get leave for the more important matches. John Briggs, now at Oxford, is also a hurdler of possibilities, but we cannot expect him to be able to turn out until the end of the term. As far as the Juniors are concerned our strength is rather unknown although we have a large number who are interested in Field Events. Doug Whitehead, who was very promising last year in the Javelin and Shot, is now in the Forces and will probably have difficulty in getting along for matches. John Morrison should show improvement in the Shot. Terry Batemen, our new Field Events Hon. Secretary, needs all your support in his first season to make it a really successful one. So you are expected to rally round him not only to improve your own performances but that of the Club in general. Your coaches for the Field Events have felt that some have not made as much use of their services as they would have liked but it is still not too late. Therefore, if you are really keen on improving your performances, contact them and you will find they are willing to give the benefit of their advice. The biggest day for Field Events is the Polytechnic "Sward Trophy" meeting at Chiswick on May 14th. Every event is included and we have to provide two men for each so it is expected you will get down to training immediately. This is followed by the County Championships on June 4th. We should like to see these Championships really well supported. Even if you cannot hope to get a place there is always a standard medal to be aimed at. The Kinnaird Trophy and the Waddilove Trophy now include most Field Events and we must have strong teams to support the runners. The Club Championships are fixed for August 6th at Tooting. All the way through the season there will be inter-club matches in which Field Events will be included as well as handicaps at all events for which we expect your full support. A number of Open Meetings are including Field Events handicaps and our support of these is needed. Not only will it give you added opportunity for competition but only by this means can the country discover new talent. Details of these meetings can be obtained during the season from the Hon. Secretary or Captain. items.sum: The Junior Captain and sprint coach Frank Simmons writes to the juniors about coaching, the A.A.A. Junior Relay, the P.T. class and Sunday rambles for the coming track season.
items.s: Frank Simmons Writes The Junior Captain and sprint coach Frank Simmons writes to the juniors about coaching, the A.A.A. Junior Relay, the P.T. class and Sunday rambles for the coming track season. FRANK SIMMONS WRITES. Dear Juniors, This is a reminder to you all that the summer season is fast approaching, which means quite a lot of you will be thinking of returning to the track. Some of you have already met me, some have yet to meet me, but to all I will be pleased to see you. I may as well tell you now that I am your junior sprint coach and that I work in close co-operation with George Clay, who is our chief coach. For Field Events Juniors, Charlie Jones and Bill Sutton are your coaches. Incidently, you did not make enough use of them last summer, so perhaps you did not do as well as you thought. This can be remedied by you alone, by turning out for coaching regularly. Micky Pyer is middle distance coach and if you pay attention to him you will do well, as I am sure if you have any running in you Micky will help you to put ti to the best use. To the sprinters, George Clay and I have ambitions but can only achieve them if you pull your weight. We have had a crack at the 4 x 110 yds. A.A.A. Junior Relay and only just failed. We want it this year and with your help we will get it. Also I want more to endeavour to enter into County and other individual championships. In short, we want to make our Club feared at shorter distances as the Cross Country boys are and our walkers are over their distances. I must warn you that the preliminary training may be boring but stick it as it all leads to bigger things. Who knows, you may be Belgrave's first Olympic Sprint Champion. I know I am aiming high but it can be done and the coach's job is to help you. Tuesday evening P.T. class under George Clay is going well at Belgrave Hall, but again I would like to see more of you there. It is designed to help you. To all the juniors, all-day Sunday rambles are taking place fortnightly and again I would urge you to come along. Charlie Jones leads and I can assure you of a very good time in good company. Wishing you all a very good track season and assuring you of the help of all your coaches. YOUR JUNIOR CAPTAIN. items.sum: Dave Martin-Shepherd on the season's socials at Belgrave Hall, followed by a report of the Annual Dinner at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction, where Tommy Green presented his trophy to Harry Churcher.
items.s: Social Section Dave Martin-Shepherd on the season's socials at Belgrave Hall, followed by a report of the Annual Dinner at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction, where Tommy Green presented his trophy to Harry Churcher. SOCIAL SECTION Dave Martin-Shepherd writes:— May I say how enjoyable it has been to see the Club members with their wives and friends at the Socials held at Belgrave Hall during this season. The support given by wives and friends to the sport in the afternoon and to the social in the evening make these occasions something to remember. I should like to take this opportunity to thank all who have assisted me, especially those who helped at the Boxing Day Party cabaret and nearly did for me at the same time. I do feel that the social side of the Club is very important and that it all goes to make Belgrave such a formidable power that it is in athletics. If you have not been to a social may I admit that we have always expected both you and your friends so what about it next season? * * * The Annual Dinner which was held at the Express Hall, Clapham Junction on Saturday, November 6th was again a huge success and the hall was filled to capacity. President Bill Webb must have felt particularly proud presiding over such a gathering which included many well known administrators in both walking and running world and not forgetting the many well known "champions." It was very pleasing to have with us our Olympic Champion, Tommy Green, and his wife, and the opportunity was taken to get him to present to Harry Churcher the handsome trophy he has given to the Club for the outstanding Club performance of the year. Tom Cotton "Esquire" was a worthy toastmaster. Our thanks are indeed due to our Social Secretary, "Dave," for the splendid evening he put on for us. The dance following was very ably conducted by Bert Ellsey. items.s: Editorial The new co-editors thank retiring editor Harry Parker, now President of the E.C.C.U., and promise improvements including a suggestion page. Dear Fellow Belgravians, We humbly present to you the Belgravian issue for November, 1949. In doing so we first of all give thanks to your past Editor, Harry Parker. Many onerous duties have come Harry's way during his career with Belgrave, extending over many years and all he has tackled with great enthusiasm and with remarkable achievements. He is not the kind of person to relinquish his commitments without very good reason, but now he finds his official duties in the service of athletics at least one too many, and he has been obliged with very great regret to hand the editorship over to new co-editors. As we all know Harry has certainly plenty on his plate and always has had and now that he is President of the E.C.C.U., he finds it hard to carry on as Editor. In congratulating him on his great honour, we also thank him for his great work to the club. As for ourselves, your new co-editors, we follow in the wake of Harry Hare, Ben Knifton, Alf Harley, Gordon Doubleday, Freddie Bradnum and Harry Parker. We are fully conscious of the great work and standards built up and maintained by our predecessors and we assure you of our best endeavours to keep up this standard. We have several ideas for the possible improvement of our magazine which we hope you will all approve but, as with this issue we are endeavouring to bring all reports up-to-date, pressure of space prevents us introducing new ideas on this occasion. We do intend, however, to issue another Belgravian at a very early date and to include these ideas, chief among which will be a "Suggestion page," and we ask those of you who have any suggestions, to let us have them in as brief a letter as possible, but let us get this issue among you first and we hope you will find the next one and subsequent issues interesting, entertaining and topical. Best wishes, Your EDITORS. Harry Parker Harry Parker retiring Editor of The Belgravian; President of the E.C.C.U. items.sum: Report of the club's 1949 Annual General Meeting, at which Bill Webb was re-elected President and officers' reports were heard.
items.s: Annual General Meeting—October 8th, 1949 Report of the club's 1949 Annual General Meeting, at which Bill Webb was re-elected President and officers' reports were heard. The attendance at this meeting was not as large as was hoped nor as large as we have the right to expect. However, a very representative gathering of somewhere about 80-90 members assembled to elect your new officials and committee and to define the club policy for the year 1949-50. Once again our popular President, Bill Webb, was elected to the premier office of the club and this was received with unanimous acclamation. Secretary Alf Harley's report struck a very optimistic note in spite of one or two reverses during the past season. In reading his report we had a moment or two of thought for the passing of three of our club members: dear old Charlie Cook, Tom Sullivan and Rowland Rowbottom, which we all regret. The Hon. Treasurer's report showed us that although we were spending much more money than we received in ordinary receipts and subscriptions, we were able to balance our club budget through the efforts of the Supporters' Club. The Building Fund is in an extremely healthy state and a word of appreciation was given to Les Cohen and his supporters. Our Treasurer, Syd King, has done a wonderful job in carrying on after that great treasurer, Bill Webb. We all thank him for his work and congratulate him on his achievements. We were sorry and considerably concerned, however, when he warned us that this would be his last year of office. Under the capable chairmanship of Bill Webb the meeting progressed. Your officers and committee were duly elected and during the ensuing phase under the heading of "Other Business," the future policy of the club was discussed in a most rational and democratic manner. One left the meeting convinced that the management of the club was again in most capable hands and with a feeling of confidence for the season 1949-50. items.sum: Stage-by-stage account of Belgrave's win in the Brighton road relay of April 1949, the club's sixth win in the race.
items.s: The "Brighton" Relay held April 2nd, 1949 Stage-by-stage account of Belgrave's win in the Brighton road relay of April 1949, the club's sixth win in the race. RUNNING NOTES Starting from Mitcham, our runner on the first stage to Purley was Derrick Burfitt. He did well to finish 5th in 30 mins. 6 secs. On the next stage to Merstham, Ted Stimpson held his place and his time was 27.25. Then Frank Abberton tackled the up-hill stage through Redhill and ran a fine race to take us up into 2nd place with a time of 23.9. On the next stage, Jack Brown took us in front and running well clocked 28.7. Len Herbert went off on the 5th stage which had been slightly altered. Jimmy Wood, our Poly. member, caught and passed him but Len managed to hang on to second place with a time of 25.29 and handed over to Albert Frost who did well in putting up the fastest time for that leg which is now only just over 2 miles and his time of 10.51 kept us in second place. Vern Blowfield went off on the long stage to Handcross and soon passed his man to put us in the lead once again. His time was 31.25. Len Marchant was our next but he lost the lead to Green of Reading and clocked 21.40 for his stage. Eddie Short went off on the up-hill climb to Patcham. He passed the leader and in clocking 21.34 did the second fastest time and gave us a lead of 11 secs. over our nearest rivals. Bull Lucas, running the last stage, as usual, did not give his opponents any chance of getting on his shoulder and although Green of Birchfield took his team into second place, Bill finished an easy winner and moreover did second fastest time of 17.49 for his leg. The order for finishing was 1, Belgrave, 3 hrs. 57 mins. 35 secs; 2, Birchfield, 3.57.52; 3, Tipton H., 3.58.35. This makes our 6th win in this classic road race, a feat which no other club has performed and moreover, is our second series of three wins in a row as we won in 1934-5-6 and then again in 1947-8-9. items.label: No. 106
items.sum: Track match at Tooting in which South London Harriers narrowly beat Belgrave in both senior and junior contests, with club handicap results.
items.s: Match v. South London H.—May 7th Track match at Tooting in which South London Harriers narrowly beat Belgrave in both senior and junior contests, with club handicap results. Held at Tooting, this was our opening fixture of the summer season and we had senior and junior events with a few club handicaps on the programme. The senior match was a very close affair and our visitors won by the very narrow margin of 2 points. They also won the junior match by 5 points. Mike Broadbent finished second to Grieve in the 100 yards. John Cope was second to Pugh in the 440 and we had first two home in the 880 in Len Marchant and Jack Brown. Bill Lucas won the mile and Eddie Short won the two miles, beating Ted Stimpson. George Powell's win in the javelin, was our only success in the field events side and we also won the medley relay. In the junior match our only winner on the track was Alan Sexton in the 220 yards, but a new member in H. R. Delger, won the javelin and we also won the 4 x 110 yards' relay. Final scores were: Senior.—S.L.H., 63 points; Bels., 61 points. Junior.—S.L.H., 25 points; Bels., 20 points. Handicap events:.— 100 yards: 1, A. Law (11); 2, D. Clements (11); 3, P. Morrison (7½). In the mile handicap a good crowd turned out and after Jack Brown looked like running through the field, he was held off on the final lap by Alf Orton who used his head as well as his legs. Placings: 1, A. H. Orton (135); 2, J. Brown (50); 3, L. Adams (110). Time: 4 mins. 17.8 secs. The two miles' walk was a scratch race with a handicap in conjunction and the eventual winner was our old friend Charlie Speechley with S. James second and P. Wilson, third. items.h: Match v. Ealing Harriers and Walton A.C.—May 14th
items.sum: Gordon Stewart Trophy match at Drayton Green won by Walton A.C., with Belgrave second and Ealing third.
items.s: Match v. Ealing Harriers and Walton A.C.—May 14th Gordon Stewart Trophy match at Drayton Green won by Walton A.C., with Belgrave second and Ealing third. Once again we visited the Drayton Green Track for the inter club contest for the "Gordon Stewart" Trophy, promoted by the local club. We congratulate Walton on their win, but as they had two Olympic men in their team we were not disgraced. Once again the two short sprints proved our undoing and we had to run Alan Sexton in the 100 yards in order to put up a show. Bill Lucas won the mile with A. Bedford second and Derek Burfitt gave Nankeville a good run in the half mile. In the two miles team race we had the first three home, with Jack Brown, Vern Blowfield and Len Marchant finishing in line. We lost the Medley Relay where John Cope tried hard to hold Nankeville over the first 880 but the Walton man gave his team the lead which they maintained to the end. Final scores were: 1st, Walton A.C., 34 points; 2nd, Belgrave H., 29 points; Ealing H., 11 points. Also on the programme were a few junior events and Walton again proved successful in these by scoring 27 points to our 18 and Ealing's 10. George Stace ran well in the mile, and Brian Rice ran second in the half mile. Dave Marshall won the 220 yards in fine style in 23.8. Alan Sexton Alan Sexton ran in the 100 yards Bill Lucas Bill Lucas won the mile A. Bedford A. items.sum: Triangular track match at Stompond Lane in which Belgrave and Walton A.C. tied on 56 points with T.V.H. third.
items.s: Match v. Walton A.C. and Thames Valley H.—May 21st Triangular track match at Stompond Lane in which Belgrave and Walton A.C. tied on 56 points with T.V.H. third. On May 21st we visited Stompond Lane for a triangular match. Here again a few junior events were included in the programme, also a 120 yards hurdles event and the home club scored in these events. They also did well in the short sprints with Lewis scoring a double and our only placed man in these events was Les Christmas, third in the 220. R. C. Sharp, running in the 440 yards, gained third place. Len Marchant put up a new ground record in the 880 yards when he beat Alec Olney in 1 min. 58 secs. Olney, however, won the mile with A. Bedford fourth and in the 2 miles Reg. Ruddick beat off the challenge of L. Field of T.V.H. to win in 9 mins. 56 secs. Our Latvian member, A. Bergvalds, was second in the shot and then won the discus throw and should prove a great help to this branch of the club. N. Gibson was second in the high jump and evergreen George Powell was second in the javelin event. We gained third place in the 4 x 110 yards relay and the final scores were: Belgrave and Walton A.C. 56 points each, T.V.H. 49, a very closely contested match and much enjoyed by all, including our supporters who turned up in good numbers. items.s: Junior Match at Croydon Return junior match against Whitgift Middle School on 30 May, won by the school 52 points to 20, several of whose placers were Belgrave members. The return match against the Whitgift Middle School was held on May 30th and a good crowd of our youngsters made the trip. Our only winner of the evening was John Morrison in the 440 yards. Wolton was second in the 880 and Hazel second in the mile. Sexton and Marshall running for their school, again completed a double for the first two places in the 100 and 220 yards and the school also won both the relay races. Cooper and Stinton who were first and second for the school in the high jump are also members of our club and so it can be seen that although we lost the match, our club members were well to the fore. items.s: Surrey County Championships Belgrave members' placings at the Surrey County senior and junior championships, including county records for Alan Sexton, John Grey and Len Herbert. The Senior and Junior Championships, with one or two exceptions were held at Motspur Park on June 4th when the club did quite well and the result of the club's coaching methods was clearly seen. Alan Sexton performed a double in winning the 100 and 220 yards and in the latter event he set up a new county record of 22.7 secs. Another club member set up a new county record when John Grey, in the Junior Discus, recorded a throw of 137 ft. 3 ins. The 3 miles championship was held at Tooting on July 6th and Len Herbert set up a new county record in the fast time of 14 mins. 38.6 secs. Bill Lucas unfortunately had to retire with leg trouble, otherwise we may have had the first two home. We are glad to see Len Herbert getting back to form as he had a disappointing season over the country and we hope that he will keep it up and lead our lads in their effort to regain our lost title of National Champions. items.h: A.A.A. Southern Senior Championships at Hove on June 25th
items.sum: Belgrave performances at the A.A.A. Southern Championships at Hove, including Harry Churcher retaining his 2 miles walk title and a junior relay win.
items.s: A.A.A. Southern Senior Championships at Hove on June 25th Belgrave performances at the A.A.A. Southern Championships at Hove, including Harry Churcher retaining his 2 miles walk title and a junior relay win. In the 100 yards, Broadbent won his heat in 10.7; qualified in the second round and was third in a 10.4 final. Cope was third in his 880 yards' heat. In the mile Marchant qualified in 4.31 and Burfitt in 4 mins 33 secs. In the final Burfitt was fourth and Marchant sixth. Len Herbert gained second place in the 3 miles after a great effort in the last lap. Bill Lucas was third and Jimmy Wood gained a "standard" in seventh place. Harry Churcher easily retained his 2 miles' walk title in 14 mins. 35 secs. In the Junior 4 x 110 yards relay our team comprising: Marshall, Tebbutt, Rae and Sexton, in that order, won their heat in 45,5 secs. items.sum: Belgravians' performances at the 1949 A.A.A. Championships, including Harry Churcher's 7 miles walk win and Charlie Smart's standard medal.
items.s: A.A.A. Championships at White City—July 16th Belgravians' performances at the 1949 A.A.A. Championships, including Harry Churcher's 7 miles walk win and Charlie Smart's standard medal. On Friday evening Michael Broadbent competed in Heat 1 of the 100 yards and was beaten by Mac Bailey in the fast time of 9.9 secs. He qualified to run in the second round on Saturday afternoon but was 5th in a 10.2 secs. heat! Geoff Jarvis won his heat in the 440 yards hurdles in 56.9 secs, and was third in the final won in 56.7 secs. In the 880 yards John Cope was fifth in his heat. In the mile, Derrick Burfitt won his heat in 4.20, but in the final was seventh in 4 min. 19 secs. Marchant and John Brown also competed. Charlie Smart made a gallant effort in the 6 miles on Friday evning and eventually finished fifth in 30 min. 42 secs., thus gaining a standard medal. Ruddock and Towndrow also ran. Harry Churcher won the 7 miles walk in 52 min.41 secs. on the Saturday morning after a deluge of rain which left the track waterlogged. Len Herbert was sixth in the 3 miles in 14 min. 37 secs. Both Smart and Ruddock had another "bash" but after their gruelling 6 miles on Friday only Smart gained a standard. The 2 miles walk was held at Birmingham on July 29th and Harry Churcher was beaten 10 yards by the Swede, Borgesson. items.h: Match v. Cambridge H. and Dartford H.—July 27th
items.sum: Report of the match at Charlton Park lost narrowly to Cambridge Harriers, with the junior match also lost to Cambridge.
items.s: Match v. Cambridge H. and Dartford H.—July 27th Report of the match at Charlton Park lost narrowly to Cambridge Harriers, with the junior match also lost to Cambridge. This was held at Charlton Park and after a very close tussle with the home club, they won by the narrow margin of 2 points. Basil Walden was second in the 100 yards and Lionel Grimshaw won the 220. Jim Heathfield was third in the 440, John Cope won the 880 in 2 mins. 1.6 secs., while Bill Lucas won the mile in 4 mins. 30.2 secs. Charlie Smart, home on leave from Germany, turned out in the 2 miles and clocked 9 mins. 45 secs. to win a good race with Ted Stimpson second. We won the medley relay, but Cambridge gained first places in all three field events and this finally decided the match in their favour. Final scores were: Cambridge H., 47 points; Belgrave H., 45 points; Dartford H., 7 points. In the junior match we gained second place in the 100 yards, also in the 220 and were third in the 880. Ken Hill was second in the mile. Ian Law second in the discus and E. Gowland second in the javelin. Scores were Cambridge H., 26 points; Belgrave H., 24 points; Dartford H., 15 points. items.s: Final Club Track Meeting—September 17th Report of Belgrave's final handicap meeting of the season at Tooting Bec on 17 September. The final handicap meeting of the season was held at Tooting Bec on Saturday, September 17th, and although the entry for the 3 miles run was up to standard, the other events on the programme were not too well supported. The final of the 100 yards was a good race and Clements just beat Kemp with Mitchell third. The 880 yards saw Ken Cuff beat A. Tapley by about one foot with J. S. Tranter third. The mile race for unattached novices only attracted four entries and P. W. Adams, a younger brother of our own runner, displayed promising form in winning this event. In the 2 miles walk, Harry Churcher walked in fine style and eventually finished second to Joe Scamell, with George Oliver third. In the 300 yards, Alan Sexton was on scratch mark and duly qualified for the final by winning his heat. The final saw the field well away but Alan went after them and on coming into the straight came through strongly to win a great race in 32.3 secs. R. Holtum, a new member was second with Johnny Morrison third. The 3 miles run was the main event on the programme with Jack Brown, the back marker off 60 yards and the limit man on 500. C. Walker who won our novice road race last winter, was off 120 yards and running strongly he eventually took the lead followed by Len Marchant and they finished in that order with Rene Howell, our Poly. member, third off 160 yards. Eddie Short lost a shoe but pluckily kept going and Archie Bedford came through to finish a good fourth. Jack Shields and Ken England were also well up and a new member in J. H. Braggington also did well in his first club race. W. Hadley scored a good handicap double by winning the javelin and long jump events and in the former George Powell was second with A. Machell third. Alan Law was second in the long jump with Frank Simmons third. items.label: No. 106
items.sum: Terry Bateman's review of Belgrave's 1949 field events season, highlighting Geoff Jarvis, John Grey, Bergvalds and Peter Lowe.
items.s: FIELD EVENTS REVIEW Terry Bateman's review of Belgrave's 1949 field events season, highlighting Geoff Jarvis, John Grey, Bergvalds and Peter Lowe. Although the year has brought a slight improvement in the standard of field events it has been due to outstanding individual efforts rather than to improved general performances. However, our juniors show great promise and we must see they are given every encouragement. One of the outstanding and commendable performances of the season was the 440 yards hurdles run by Geoff Jarvis in 56.7 secs. which gave him third place in the A.A.A. Championships. This was followed by another good performance in his winning the R.A.F. Championship and in being chosen as reserve for England v. France match for the same event. Previously Geoff had concentrated on the high hurdles and the change to 440 yards has obviously been most successful. Another outstanding performance was that of John Grey's discus throw of 137 ft. 3 ins. which won him the Surrey County Junior Championship and broke the existing record by about 18 ft. He also gained a standard medal in the A.A.A. Junior Championships. Our weakest events have been the high and long jumps. Conditions were not improved when mid-way through the season we lost the services of Steve Gibson, one of our most promising high jumpers who went into hospital for an operation on an old war wound. We take this opportunity of wishing him a speedy recovery and hope to see him out at the winter training sessions John Sinton a junior who has given good support to our senior matches is to be congratulated on his 5 ft. 6 ins. jump in the Police match at Imber Court. Both the juniors, Bob Cooper and Jim Purdy, have been jumping well and show promise. We were not too successful in either the Svard or Kinnaird meetings. One of the best performances was that of Harry Delger at the Kinnaird meeting when he threw the junior javelin about 154 feet to gain third place. Bergvalds was the outstanding performer in the club championships. He won the discus and shot, and was third in the javelin. His discus throw of 123 ft. 8½ ins. set up a new club record. Peter Lowe established a new club record in the hop, step and jump, with an effort of 41 ft. 5 ins. Charlie Melchoir retained his javelin title with Les Higgins as runner-up. Our old stalwart, George Powell, has been consistently throwing the javelin over 140 ft. in matches and has been a source of inspiration to younger aspirants. It is intended to resume the field events training periods through the winter months at Tooting on alternate Saturday afternoons. items.s: JUNIOR NOTES F. Simmons's letter to the juniors reviewing their county and Southern successes and announcing winter P.T. and Sunday strolls; it gives J. Grey's county record discus as 137 ft. 8 ins., where the field events review on page 14 prints 137 ft. 3 ins. Dear Juniors, The summer season is now finished and it is with pleasure that I say thank you for your support in both matches and in championships. We had a successful season ending in successes in County and Southern County Championships. Our successes in the County Championship were: A. Sexton, 100 yards in 10.5 secs.; Equals County record. 220 yards in 22.7; New County record. D. Marshall, 100 yards, third; 220 yards, second. Picton, 220 yards. County standard. J. Grey, Discus, 1st. New County record; 137 ft. 8 ins. Southern Counties: A. Sexton, 220 yards, 1st, 23 secs. We had three in the final of the 220 yards and John Morrison gained his Southern standard in the 440 yards. In addition we won the Southern Counties 4 x 110 yards relay. Our congratulations to Desmond Mullen on winning the Irish Junior 100 yards and his second in the 220. Some of you did not do as well as you hoped, but keep trying and success will come and when it does it will be all the sweeter. Some of our junior pals will be leaving our section to go forward to the seniors and our best wishes for continued success goes with them. To all new recruits to our section we give a “ Belgrave ” welcome and assure you all of a healthy and happy time. To our cross-country juniors, we wish you every success in the coming months. It is hoped, all juniors who can possibly attend, will come along to our winter P.T. class at Belgrave Hall. Details will be available later, also Charlie Jones and I are arranging all day strolls from November until April every Sunday, which we hope you will all make an effort to come along to. They are very good for you, in fact, the senior successes were built up on their strolling and I see no reason why you cannot do the same. The strolls will be worked out so that the cost will suit everybody's pocket. I thoroughly understand that some of you have home studies, but when you can make it, come along, you can be sure of a welcome and a good time too. In conclusion, on behalf of the juniors, I convey their congratulations to Harry Churcher on his winning the A.A.A. 7 miles' walk again and also on his new world's record. F. SIMMONS. F. Simmons F. items.label: No. 106
items.sum: Review of Belgrave's 1949 race walking season: Met. W.C. 15, Chichester–Portsmouth, club and national championships, Harry Churcher's records and titles, and the London to Brighton walk.
e: Belgrave Harriers Club 20 Miles' Walk Championship
items.s: WALKING NOTES Review of Belgrave's 1949 race walking season: Met. W.C. 15, Chichester–Portsmouth, club and national championships, Harry Churcher's records and titles, and the London to Brighton walk. Looking back over the season which has just finished, we certainly have not disgraced ourselves. Our wins in Open Races in the South have been up to our usual standard and we have been placed in two of the Senior National Championships. That we can do better there is no doubt, especially do we need some more young members and it is hoped that the coming season will see an improvement in this direction. Continuing our activities, following the National 10, three teams were entered for the Met. W.C. 15 miles at Regent's Park, but alas, before any great distance had been covered, Charlie Churcher was ruled out and our chances of success thereby greatly reduced. This race seems to be very unfortunate for us, as like last year, we suffered more than the usual disqualifications. These included Pat Sapcote and Jack Baker. The unusual distance of the race got the team selectors guessing with the result that two of our “ B ” team men finished before the second “ A ” team man. Outstanding was Bob Readman who held the lead throughout the greater part of the race, but on the last lap he tired rather badly and dropped back to third place. With a team score of 64 points we were very surprised to find that we gained third place. In the Chichester to Portsmouth race on Easter Saturday, Charlie Churcher repeated his brilliant performance of last year by winning the individual honour. As we did not send a very strong team, it was not surprising that we were unable to get better than third place, 9 points behind the winners, Woodford Green. The following Saturday we held our own Club 20 Miles' Championship. As usual, being the first 20 of the season, a number of the starters failed to finish the course, but the 14 who completed the distance walked exceptionally well. Veteran Jack Bidgood, after 20 years with the club, succeeded in winning his first Championship after a well-judged race, followed by Pat Sapcote and Charlie Churcher. And so we came to the National 20 and from the performances of our walkers in the Club 20 it seemed that we had a reasonable chance of success. Unfortunately Bert Webb was unable to make the journey to Manchester and we were without any knowledge of the capabilities of the Sheffield boys over the longer distance. The weather, for Manchester, was extremely good, in fact, no rain fell throughout the day. At the start the two Sheffield lads, Allen and Proctor, made a quick getaway and joined by Lloyd Johnson, set up a good pace. Lloyd however, did not last with them for long and soon began to drop back. Most of our lads walked extremely well and were ably assisted by Harry Churcher, Syd Roberts and Percy Wilson, but despite all their efforts, they were unable to do better than second place, with Charlie Churcher taking third individual honour. Competition for the Nijmegen Shield was very keen. Sheffield being successful, with Woodford Green second and ourselves third. In a new promotion this year, the Watford 25, we entered a small team and succeeded in gaining third place in both the scratch and handicap sections. The last National Championship of the season, the 50 Kilos. was held from the Police Sports Club at Chigwell over a very stiff course. The weather, which was very warm, added to the trials of the walkers and of 73 starters, no less than 31 retired without completing the full distance. These included Charlie Churcher, who developed leg trouble, Pat Sapcote, Fred Herring, Jack Wakeley and Don Heath, so that by the end of the race we had just a bare four left, who finished in fourth position, 2 points behind Woodford. For the Eastleigh A.C. 50 Kilos. on July 16th, Pat Sapcote was unable to make the journey at the last minute, thus depriving us of one of our best men. However, Bert Clayton sprung a great surprise by leading all the way through and eventually winning the individual race, and although the rest of the team walked exceedingly well, they had to be content with second place to Surrey W.C. Jack Bidgood also won a style prize, and Bert Clayton was second in the handicap. On August 23rd we were invited to field a team in Surrey W.C.'s 6 miles road race at Tooting Bec Common. Despite the fact that the fixture did not appear on our summer programme, 12 of our walkers turned out and after a very interesting race, Surrey just managed to win by 103 points to 107. So much for the road walks. On the track Harry Churcher, as is now well known, succeeded in lowering his world's record time of last year for the 5 miles. Walking in excellent style, Harry lapped the track time after time in almost identical times, eventually clipping 10.4 secs. off his time at Motspur Park. In addition to this he succeeded in taking the Surrey County 2 miles' title, the Southern Counties 2 miles title, and on a water-logged track at the White City, the 7 miles A.A.A. title. A fortnight later Harry took second place to Borgesson in the A.A.A. 2 miles but revenged his defeat in the London-Gothenburg Match a week later by winning the 7 miles at the White City in 51.2.2, his fastest time for the distance. This race prevented him from defending his Club 2 miles title and in his absence Bob McMullen, walking in very fine style, became this year's club champion. On June 22nd we had our annual mob match with Surrey W.C. on the track at Tooting, beating them by 89 points to 121, with Joe Scamell (jr.), Brian Shepherd and Mac taking the handicap awards in that order. A “ B ” team match against the Veterans A.C. at Tooting Bec on July 9th also resulted in a win for us. Our Annual Inter Club Walks of 1, 2, 3 and 4 miles proved a great success this year, no fewer than 66 walkers competing. The competition proved to be very keen, eventually resulting in a win for Woodford Green with Highgate Harriers second and us third. A number of our walkers have figured well in Open Handicaps and Veterans' Events, successes being scored by Bert East, Syd James, Charlie Speechley and young Joe Scamell. As usual our Police members figured well in the Barking to Southend Walk. Jack Bidgood was once again second with Bob Readman, Pat Sapcote and Bert Webb following him home in that order. The winning team, “ B ” Division, was completely Belgrave. On August 27th we had a 25 miles match with London Vidarians and Surrey Walking Club. This race next year is to be an Open Event and should prove a good training walk for the Brighton. The race resulted in a win for Surrey W.C. with us second. In the London to Brighton Walk on September 10th, eleven of our walkers started off on the stroke of Big Ben at seven o'clock, to be joined later by a number of supporters. In the early stages, Jack Bidgood, Bert Clayton, Jack Baker, Jack Wakeley and George Oliver, walked in a group with Don Heath and Joe Wilson not far away. Gordon Doubleday, F. Herring, Sid Spencer and Bill Urry, followed at an easier pace. Jack Bidgood eventually went away from the others and at the Chequers Horley was in ninth position. A check at Crawley (29¾ miles) showed that our men had held their positions with the exception of Jack Wakeley who had stopped for a massage. By the time Bolney was reached, Jack Bidgood had improved his position to seventh, Clayton was 16th, Baker 21st and Wilson 27th. With the retirement of Bert Martineau from the Surrey team there seemed a chance that our team would be placed and although Jack Bidgood dropped a couple of places to go back to ninth Joe Wilson moved up to 23rd and at the finish our positions were: Jack Bidgood, ninth; Bert Clayton, 16th; Joe Wilson, 21st; Jack Baker, 23rd, making a score of 62 points and just losing us the third position. So Jack Bidgood became our long-distance champion as well as holder of the 20 Miles Championship. He's a champion to be proud of. His judgment of pace and unflagging stamina throughout the race set a fine example. Bert Clayton was a worthy second and showed his grit in overcoming tiredness in the last few miles. Joe Wilson walked his best Brighton to date and came along in fine style in the latter half to finish remarkably fresh. Jack Baker pluckily stuck it out over the last half to complete the team.
